title: Low-Complexity and Resource-Efficient Design of a Streaming Channel Estimation for ZP-OTFS.
abstract: This work presents a low-complexity and resource-efficient hardware architecture for Channel Estimation (CE) in Zero-Padded Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (ZP-OTFS) systems. The proposed design reconstructs the channel impulse response in the delay–time domain through a partially parallel interpolation scheme, enabling continuous streaming while exploiting matrix sparsity to reduce computational overhead. The architecture is implemented at the Register Transfer Level (RTL) in VHDL, with functional validation performed via FPGA-in-the-Loop (FIL). A prototype on the AMD ZCU111 board demonstrates high efficiency in terms of area and power, with 44.10μs latency and 1.45μJ per-frame energy, quantifying performance unavailable in prior SDR-only implementations. These results confirm the suitability of the proposed architecture for integration into complete OTFS receivers that target high-mobility wireless communication scenarios.

title: Live Demonstration: A Portable Pressure Imaging System for Convenient and Ubiquitous Lumbar Disc Herniation Screening.
abstract: Early screening for lumbar disc herniation (LDH) remains challenging due to the high cost and limited accessibility of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). To address this issue, we develop an automated screening system based on seated biomechanical analysis, capable of performing seated pressure acquisition, feature analysis, and LDH risk assessment. The system first captures a pressure map of the user’s buttocks in a standardized seated posture using a custom-designed, highly sensitive flexible pressure array. Mechanical and statistical features that characterize seated asymmetry and balance are then extracted from the pressure map. These features are subsequently fed into a trained machine learning model to predict and display risk assessment results. This approach enables large-scale, low-cost lumbar health screening and provides a practical tool for the early detection of LDH risk. Key technical specifications of the system are as follows: sensor dimensions: 40 cm × 40 cm; array configuration: 32 × 32; measurement range: 1 – 50 kg; sampling frame rate: 3.3 fps; prediction duration: 30 s; weight: 2 kg; thickness:100Ω. A demo video of the proposed pressure imaging system, including recordings of both real-world usage and screen output, is available at: https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.30225178

title: Screening of Lumbar Disc Herniation Using Buttock Pressure Imaging System.
abstract: Lumbar disc herniation (LDH) diagnosis relies on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), which is costly and not widely accessible. This paper presents a cost-effective screening alternative based on buttock pressure distribution. We develop a custom flexible pressure imaging system with a novel parallel readout circuit, which is validated to exhibit high linearity (R2=0.999), excellent spatial consistency, and stable performance over 1,000 loading cycles. Using this system, buttock pressure distribution characteristics (PDC) are modeled by an α-stable distribution to extract features quantifying asymmetry (β), center (μ), and dispersion (σ). These features are used to train a classifier that achieved 85.71% accuracy in identifying LDH on a clinical cohort.

title: Probabilistic Sensing: Intelligence in Data Sampling.
abstract: Extending the intelligence of sensors to the data-acquisition process - deciding whether to sample or not - can result in transformative energy-efficiency gains. However, making such a decision in a deterministic manner involves risk of losing information. Here we present a sensing paradigm that enables making such a decision in a probabilistic manner. The paradigm takes inspiration from the autonomous nervous system and employs a probabilistic neuron (p-neuron) driven by an analog feature extraction circuit. The response time of the system is on the order of microseconds, over-coming the sub-sampling-rate response time limit and enabling real-time intelligent autonomous activation of data-sampling. Validation experiments on active seismic survey data demonstrate lossless probabilistic data acquisition, with a normalized mean squared error of 0.41%, and 93% saving in the active operation time of the system and the number of generated samples.

title: Double-Clock Architecture for Small-Duty-Cycle DC-DC Converters.
abstract: Many applications pose stringent requirements on the voltage-conversion-ratio (VCR) that a DC-DC converter should cover, requiring it to reliably synthesize very small duty-cycles. One of such applications is the power management of Li-ion battery powered Active Matrix Organic Light Emitting Diode (AMOLED) displays. In this article a double-clock architecture for current-mode DC-DC converters is proposed, which guarantees high-quality regulated rails. By means of a small-signal model it is shown that the proposed architecture also provides benefits in terms of jitter sensitivity. Measurements of a fabricated boost converter in a 180nm technology validate the architecture.

title: A 3-day ASIC Design Hands-on with the Minimal Fab.
abstract: Because ASIC design and fabrication require substantial cost and long lead times, they are not suitable for student laboratory courses; this has become one reason the number of students aspiring to enter the semiconductor field has not grown. Using a short-turn, low-cost Structured-ASIC design and fabrication approach we call the Agile-Chip Platform, we proposed a student experiment that can be completed quickly and inexpensively, and we piloted an exercise to design and fabricate a simple ring oscillator. Although this experiment requires relatively little knowledge of electronic circuits and allows students to easily experience chip implementation, it remains far from the full design process of a practical digital IC. In this paper, we report on an experiment in which we used the Agile-Chip Platform to implement digital logic circuits on a gate array, connect them to an embedded RISC-V CPU, and build a small-scale system-on-a-chip (SoC) that can be powered on and functionally verified. The circuits to be implemented on the gate array can be designed using a standard flow — from HDL description, through logic synthesis, to automatic layout. Because the current Agile-Chip Platform performs interconnect wiring using only five metal layers, some challenges arise during the automatic routing stage; however, these can be resolved with a few hours of work. In a trial conducted in August 2025, six participants independently designed and implemented their own circuits within three days. Two weeks later, the packaged chips were tested on a dedicated debug board, and five different chips were confirmed to operate as designed.

title: Training slow silicon neurons to control extremely fast robots with spiking reinforcement learning.
abstract: Air hockey demands split-second decisions at high puck velocities, a challenge we address with a compact network of spiking neurons running on a mixed-signal analog/digital neuromorphic processor. By co-designing hardware and learning algorithms, we train the system to achieve successful puck interactions through reinforcement learning in a remarkably small number of trials. The network leverages fixed random connectivity to capture the task's temporal structure and adopts a local e-prop learning rule in the readout layer to exploit event-driven activity for fast and efficient learning. The result is real-time learning with a setup comprising a computer and the neuromorphic chip in-the-loop, enabling practical training of spiking neural networks for robotic autonomous systems. This work bridges neuroscience-inspired hardware with real-world robotic control, showing that brain-inspired approaches can tackle fast-paced interaction tasks while supporting always-on learning in intelligent machines.

title: Efficient VLSI Architecture for Finding Maximum Value and Its Corresponding Index.
abstract: This paper proposes an area and power-efficient VLSI architecture for finding the maximum value from an array of inputs using bitwise parallel AND (BPA) operations. The proposed BPA architecture has a fixed critical delay path independent of input size, ensuring a scalable operating frequency, with a trade-off in latency compared to existing architectures. ASIC synthesis results show that the proposed BPA design achieves a reduction of 6% to 13% in area delay product and 10% to 21% in power delay product for 16-bit and 6-bit fixed-point implementations, respectively. These results confirm that BPA architecture provides improved efficiency with lower area and power consumption compared to state-of-the-art designs.

title: A Scaling Annealing Method for Combinatorial Optimization in Asynchronous Memristive Hopfield Network.
abstract: The memristive Hopfield neural networks (HNNs) can greatly accelerate the solving of combinatorial optimization problems. However, efficient annealing methods are required to prevent HNNs from converging to sub-optimal solutions. In this paper, we propose a novel scaling annealing (ScA) method and circuit design using the intrinsic stochasticity of the memristors to mitigate the local minima problem. Specifically, asynchronous updates are employed with the ScA method to prevent the hardware overhead from going out of control as the problem size grows. Based on the classical max-cut problems, simulation results show that on a 60-node problem, ScA finds the global minimum with 5.4× higher accuracy than the HNN without annealing. In addition, compared to the prior annealing schemes for memristive HNNs, the ScA method exhibits a better overall solution performance, and achieves 9.5× reduction in the annealing circuit area overhead for a 60-node problem.

title: Residual-Free Image Reconstruction from HEVC for Compressed-Domain Visual Analytics.
abstract: Conventional video analytics systems require full pixel-domain decoding before object detection or classification, incurring significant computational overhead. This study introduces a novel method for reconstructing images directly from HEVC bitstreams without residual data, enabling efficient compressed-domain processing. We propose a Gaussian-based random perturbation technique that substitutes residuals during intra-frame reconstruction, generating structurally meaningful images suitable for machine learning tasks. Our approach reconstructs images using only prediction metadata and statistically generated perturbations, bypassing the most computationally intensive component of HEVC decoding. Applied to the BIT-Vehicle dataset, our method achieves 35.60% reduction in reconstruction time compared to full decoding, while achieving near-perfect vehicle detection and 96.84% classification accuracy. By eliminating residual decoding, the proposed approach enables faster and more lightweight video analytics pipelines. Although not visually interpretable by humans, the reconstructed images retain sufficient structure for deep learning models, potentially offering benefits in privacy-conscious scenarios. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first method to fully eliminate residual decoding in HEVC for compressed-domain image reconstruction supporting object classification tasks.

title: Planting CRYSTALS-Kyber Acceleration Seeds.
abstract: CRYSTALS-Kyber (FIPS203) was one of the first post quantum cryptography schemes to be standardized by the National Institute of Standards and Technology; CRYSTALS-Kyber utilizes Montgomery reduction at the heart of the modulo reduction. Montgomery reduction traditionally is suited to computing moduli much larger than 32/64-bits. Recently a new modulo reduction method was published named Plantard reduction which allows for one less multiplication at the reduction stage. However, this does require doubling the word size of the values being calculated, in the case of CRYSTALS-Kyber increasing from 16-bit to 32-bit. In this paper we present the worlds first Plantard ISE on the Ibex RISC-V core and investigate the impact Instruction Set Extensions can have utilizing this new modulo reduction method over original methods such as Montgomery and Barrett reduction. Utilizing Plantard reduction as a set of Instruction Set Extensions, we are able to reduce the cycle counts required to compute the entire CRYSTALS-Kyber algorithm by up to 21% and reduce the cycle counts of the NTT by 1.7x and the INTT by 2.6x against the reference implementation.

title: Cross-Resolution Transfer Learning in Pixelated RF Filter Inverse Design.
abstract: Addressing the contradiction between resolution and electromagnetic (EM) simulation dataset collection efficiency in pixelated RF circuit design, this paper proposes a cross-resolution transfer learning approach for pixelated circuit design. The method achieves lossless cross-resolution migration of circuit layouts through edge anti-aliasing pixelated configurations, establishing a complete technical framework from low-resolution EM surrogate model training to high-resolution circuit design. Experimental results demonstrate that, starting from a 16×16 training dataset, the proposed method requires only an additional 13% of 32×32 samples to accurately predict arbitrary 32×32 layouts, achieving a mean squared error below 0.0032. In the validation of the 1.8-2.7GHz bandpass filter design, after migrating the low-resolution design to a 32×32 high-resolution design and further optimization, the filter performance is significantly improved. Harmonic control and roll-off characteristics are substantially enhanced, with stopband suppression superior to -17 dB up to the 4th harmonic, validating the effectiveness and practicality of this method in reducing data requirements while improving design performance.

title: Ising-ReRAM: A Low Power Ising Machine ReRAM Crossbar for NP Problems.
abstract: Computational workloads are growing exponentially, driving power consumption to unsustainable levels. Efficiently distributing large-scale networks is an NP-Complete problem equivalent to Boolean satisfiability (SAT), making it one of the core challenges in modern computation. To address this, physics and device inspired methods such as Ising systems have been explored for solving SAT more efficiently. In this work, we implement an Ising model equivalence of the 3-SAT problem using a ReRAM crossbar fabricated in the Skywater 130 nm CMOS process. Our ReRAM-based algorithm achieves 91.0% accuracy in matrix representation across iterative reprogramming cycles. Additionally, we establish a foundational energy profile by measuring the energy costs of small sub-matrix structures within the problem space, demonstrating under linear growth trajectory for combining sub-matrices into larger problems. These results demonstrate a promising platform for developing scalable architectures to accelerate NP-Complete problem solving.

title: In Simplicity There Is Strength: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of XGBoost for Generalizable SRAM Stability Prediction.
abstract: Static Random Access Memory (SRAM) is a key element in modern electronics, and predicting its stability often motivates the use of increasingly complex models. In this work, we challenge this trend by showing that simpler approaches can be highly effective. Through a series of experiments, we demonstrate that a well-tuned Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model achieves strong in-domain prediction accuracy for critical SRAM metrics including Access Disturb Margin (ADM), Write Margin (WRM) and Ireadmin. More importantly, the same model also delivers robust performance in cross-domain prediction, a task typically viewed as more challenging. To further test whether added complexity improves generalization, we design a parameter-sharing neural network (PS-NN) tailored for cross-domain transfer. Our results show that the PS-NN does not outperform the simpler XGBoost model. Taken together, these findings support a "simplicity-first" approach in electronic design automation, where the strengths of efficient models like XGBoost should be fully assessed before turning to more complex architectures. Ultimately, such prediction capabilities have the potential to transform the design process and accelerate decision-making for circuit designers.

title: Energy-Efficient Epileptic Seizure Prediction Using Spiking Neural Networks.
abstract: Early, reliable prediction of epileptic seizures from scalp EEG can materially improve patient safety, as well as enable responsive interventions. The low energy consumption of Spiking Neural Networks (SNN) makes them good candidates for wearable devices implementation. In this paper, we propose an energy-efficient seizure prediction method compatible with resource-constrained wearable devices. We developed a patient-specific SNN-based model trained and tested on the CHB-MIT scalp EEG dataset. The proposed model combines two convolutional layers with Leaky Integrate-and-Fire spiking neurons, a recurrent neural network to capture temporal dependencies, and surrogate-gradient training. A seizure-wise leave-one-out protocol is used for development and assessment. Our experimental result indicates that the proposed model attains a mean Accuracy of 93.60%, Sensitivity of 88.91%, Specificity of 98.29%, F1-Score of 91.85%, and AUROC of 0.9360, indicating accurate pre-ictal brain state detection compared to the state-of-the-art algorithms while consuming much less energy. The event-driven nature of SNNs supports the long-term goal of power-constrained, on-device seizure prediction in wearable/IoT settings.

title: Configurable p-Neurons Using Modular p-Bits.
abstract: Probabilistic bits (p-bits) have recently been employed in neural networks (NNs) as stochastic neurons with sigmoidal probabilistic activation functions. Nonetheless, there remain a wealth of other probabilistic activation functions that are yet to be explored. Here we re-engineer the p-bit by decoupling its stochastic signal path from its input data path, giving rise to a modular p-bit that enables the realization of probabilistic neurons (p-neurons) with a range of configurable probabilistic activation functions, including a probabilistic version of the widely used Logistic Sigmoid, Tanh and Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) activation functions. We present spintronic (CMOS + sMTJ) designs that show wide and tunable probabilistic ranges of operation. Finally, we experimentally implement digital-CMOS versions on an FPGA, with stochastic unit sharing, and demonstrate an order of magnitude (10x) saving in required hardware resources compared to conventional digital p-bit implementations.

title: Cryo-CMOS Antenna for Wireless Communications within a Quantum Computer Cryostat.
abstract: Scaling quantum computers from a few qubits to large numbers remains one of the critical challenges in realizing practical quantum advantage. Multi-core quantum architectures have emerged as a promising solution, enabling scalability through distributed quantum processing units (QPUs) interconnected via classical and quantum links. However, the bottleneck of wired connections persists, as densely packed wired interconnects, both vertically across temperature stages and horizontally within the same layer, introduce spatial constraints, power dissipation, and latency, which could hinder performance as the number of QPUs increases. To overcome these limitations, this work proposes a cryo-compatible on-chip differential dipole antenna operating at 28 GHz to enable short-range wireless communication within a quantum computer cryostat. Temperature-dependent material properties are incorporated to accurately capture antenna behavior at 4 K. Moreover, by embedding the antenna in a realistic cryostat structure, we evaluate the feasibility of antenna operation within the cryogenic environment. The proposed antenna achieves a reflection coefficient of -20.8 dB in free space and -18.38 dB within the cryostat, demonstrating efficient impedance matching.

title: A Front-End for Parkinsonian Tremor Detection Using Memristive Spike Encoding.
abstract: Real-time detection of Parkinsonian rest tremor is vital for assessing disease severity and evaluating therapeutic interventions such as medication and deep brain stimulation (DBS). Conventional digital pipelines often rely on microcontrollers and power-intensive processing, making them unsuitable for compact or low-power continuous monitoring applications. In this context, memristive circuits offer a promising alternative, enabling simplified and fully analog processing. This work proposes an analog front-end architecture that extracts the envelope of the tremor velocity signal through rectification, low-pass filtering, and signal conditioning. The resulting signal modulates a memristive-based oscillator (MBO), producing spike trains whose temporal structure encodes the input amplitude for downstream detection. Evaluation on representative patient recordings demonstrates that the oscillator output varies systematically across therapeutic states using the bio-inspired depolarization blocking concept, thus enabling detection directly in the analog domain. The proposed system provides a low-complexity framework for signal-driven tremor analysis.

title: Neuromorphic Sensing-and-Computing for Multi-Panel Cancer Diagnostics by Memristive Biosensors.
abstract: The investigation of memristors has promoted the development of neuromorphic devices, which play a key role in in-memory computing and brain-inspired computation. In this work, we propose, for the first time, the concept of neuromorphic sensing-and-computing out of several cancer markers by memristive biosensors. Building upon memristive biosensors, each detecting a different cancer biomarker, our design directly converts biomolecular concentrations into spiking signals by employing a unipolar volatile memristor (UVM). These spikes can then serve as the input layer of a spiking neural network (SNN). Unlike conventional single-marker assays, the proposed approach supports multi-marker integration and multi-strategy analysis. Using dual-markers assessment of prostate cancer as an example, we provide preliminary validation of cancer risk prediction, highlighting the potential of neuromorphic sensing-and-computing as a new paradigm for disease diagnosis.

title: Source Free Domain Adaptation For 3D Cross-modal Semantic Segmentation.
abstract: 3D cross-modal semantic segmentation (CMSS) is crucial for autonomous driving and robotics. Existing unsupervised domain adaptation methods align domain and modal features to handle source-target distribution differences. However, in privacy-preserving scenarios where source data is inaccessible, these methods suffer significant performance degradation. In this paper, we explore the challenging task of source free domain adaptation for 3D cross-modal semantic segmentation. We propose cross-modal matching knowledge distillation for accurate 2D-3D transfer learning by leveraging prediction consistency between point clouds, pixels, and pixel neighbors. To address prediction inconsistencies caused by different domain gaps in 2D and 3D modalities, we introduce a hyperparameter-free Modal Adaptive Pseudo-label Fusion (MAPF) that adaptively fuses 2D-3D predictions to generate accurate pseudo-labels. Experiments on three cross-modal adaptation datasets demonstrate our method achieves superior performance and surpasses datadependent UDA approaches.

title: Accelerating Audio-driven 3D Facial Animation Training with a Compressive Sensing Framework.
abstract: The training of end-to-end models for audio-driven 3D facial animation is often hindered by the significant computational overhead of direct loss computation on high-dimensional 3D mesh data. To address this efficiency bottleneck, we propose a novel compressed-domain training framework. Our method leverages the principles of Compressive Sensing to shift the loss computation from the high-dimensional vertex space to a compact, low-dimensional signal space. Extensive experiments on multiple state-of-the-art architectures demonstrate that our framework significantly accelerates the training process, with speedups ranging from 1.52x to a remarkable 9.57x, while maintaining generation quality comparable to SOTA methods. Our findings establish a superior solution that achieves an exceptional trade-off between computational efficiency and final animation quality.

title: An Efficient Optimization Framework for Netlist Partitioning by Co-optimizing Moves and Replications.
abstract: The evolution of 2.5D multi-die FPGA architectures presents significant timing closure challenges due to large inter-die communication delays. To address this, we propose an automated Electronic Design Automation (EDA) framework that transforms standard design files into a timing-aware hypergraph. Our framework then minimizes inter-die delays by synergistically co-optimizing node movement and logic replication, guided by a unified, hop-aware gain model. Experimental results on large-scale benchmarks demonstrate an average 27% reduction in total hop distance, validating the effectiveness of our partitioning strategy.

title: A Dual-Output Resonant Current-Mode Wireless Power Receiver With Shared-Inductor Energy Replenishing for Neuron Stimulation.
abstract: This paper presents a resonant current-mode (RCM) wireless power receiver achieving both normal dual-output regulation and shared-inductor energy replenishing for implantable neuron stimulation. By introducing a shared-inductor boost-converter configuration, the energy stored in one output can be directly shared to another output in proposed RCM receiver without wireless power waste. Therefore, only three transistors and three off-chip capacitors are adopted, which optimizes the efficiency and compactness. The proposed wireless power receiver is designed in a 0.18-μm BCD process and regulates two output voltages of 5V and 3V. Simulation results show that the peak power conversion efficiency reaches 90.8%. Thanks to the proposed shared-inductor energy replenishing method, the receiver extended the peak output power range by 9.4x with a maximum output power of 51mW. For a high-voltage output load switching between 0.2mA and 4mA, the transition between the normal voltage regulation and the energy replenishing is fast and smooth.

title: A Power-efficient 5x Compressive Sensing Readout IC for 3D-stacked CMOS Image Sensor.
abstract: This paper presents a power-efficient compressive sensing (CS) readout integrated circuit (IC) for 3D-stacked CMOS image sensors (CIS). The proposed readout architecture consists of a dynamic source follower (SF), a switched-capacitor (SC) multiplier, and a two-step coarse-fine SAR-SS ADC. To improve energy efficiency while ensuring image reconstruction quality, the following techniques have been introduced: First, the dynamic SF decouples its power consumption from the high pixel supply voltage, while eliminating static power during ADC conversion. Second, a deterministic measurement matrix eliminates column weight wiring and the global pseudo-random number generators (PRNG), which reduces the power and area overhead. Third, the two-step coarse-fine quantization scheme reduces the SS ADC’s input range by a factor of 8, significantly lowering the counter toggle frequency and corresponding dynamic power. Additionally, the sampling capacitors of the dynamic SF are repurposed as both the computation capacitors in the SC multiplier and the capacitive digital-to-analog converter (CDAC) of the SAR ADC, enhancing the area efficiency of column readout circuits. The proposed CS readout IC achieves 5× image compression at 60 fps while maintaining high reconstruction quality (PSNR>33.2 dB, SSIM>0.91). With a total power consumption of 268 uW, the design achieves an overall energy efficiency of 66 pJ/pixel•frame.

title: VCCU: A RISC-V-based Edge Computing Processor Capable of General-Purpose Computing and Infrared Image Processing.
abstract: Since neural network algorithms based on infrared images have been applied in many fields, the demand for edge computing devices tailored for infrared images has increased significantly in recent years. To simultaneously achieve general-purpose computing and infrared image processing in edge computing devices, we can use RISC-V as the CPU for edge computing and realize various customized data processing through instructions. Therefore, this paper proposes a RISC-V-based coprocessor named Vector Computing Co-Unit (VCCU) which integrates four core functional modules: 1) a Convolution Unit with FIFO modules for efficient data reuse and parallel convolution operations; 2) a Dot Product Unit with multi-precision Processing Elements (PEs)—each PE contains 64 4-bit multipliers configurable into 8/16/32-bit multipliers; 3) a Quantization Unit that directly quantizes 14–16-bit infrared images from the Read-Out Integrated Circuit to 8-bit; and 4) a Vector Mapping Unit that maps 3D multi-channel feature images and convolution kernels to 2D vectors. Synthesized with the 55nm process, VCCU achieves a peak performance of 168 GOPS and a peak energy efficiency of 1193 GOPS/W, while supporting 4-32-bit multi-precision computation. Its peak performance is 2.26×-34.7× higher and energy efficiency is 1.05×-2.09× higher than those of similar RISC-V edge devices.

title: Visual Geometric 6-DoF Grasping: A Multi-View Framework with Sparse RGB Observations.
abstract: Current robotic grasping systems predominantly rely on single-view RGB-D grasp detection, which critically necessitates a depth sensor. While pure multi-view RGB estimation methods have emerged recently, those largely based on Implicit Neural Representations (INRs) often confront the challenge of inaccurate geometric reconstruction, which subsequently reduces grasp prediction reliability. To address these limitations, we propose a novel Visual Geometric 6-DoF Grasping framework (VG-Grasp) that integrates sparse-view 3D reconstruction with heatmap-guided grasp generation. Leveraging transformer-based cross-view attention, our method reconstructs dense point clouds from a few RGB images and predicts stable grasp poses without requiring direct depth input. Evaluated on the GraspNet-1Billion dataset, our approach significantly outperforms existing RGB-based 6-DoF Grasping methods, especially on seen and similar objects. Real-robot experiments demonstrate a 61% grasp success rate and 83% completion rate, validating the effectiveness and practicality of our depth-free solution.

title: An Ultra-Low Power Data Retention Flip-Flop with 25.8 pW Leakage in 28 nm CMOS.
abstract: Data retention flip-flops (DR-FFs) can help processors in duty-cycled battery-powered IoT devices to maintain the state data during sleep mode, helping them quickly recover from the previous state upon wake-up to reduce latency. This paper introduces a new ultra-low-leakage balloon-based DR-FF that implements data retention using ultra-low-power (ULP) diodes with transistors biased in the super-cut-off region. Implemented in both 180 nm and 28 nm CMOS technology, the proposed DR-FF shows a 0.04 pW / 25.8 pW in sleep mode leakage power, which is more than 3× lower than prior CMOS DR-FFs. Also, it shows faster and more energy-efficient mode transitions than other balloon-based DR-FFs. The overall performance of the proposed DR-FF makes it a promising solution for low-power, duty-cycled IoT processors that require low wake-up latency.

title: A ML-based Robust Channel Estimation Enhancer Against Multi-Tone Jamming in OFDM systems.
abstract: Orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) systems rely critically on accurate channel estimation to ensure reliable communication but are highly susceptible to jamming attacks. Multi-tone jamming is particularly challenging as it provides a unified representation of diverse interference patterns through adjustable tone spacing and power allocation. Existing works, including neural network (NN)-based techniques, primarily target individual tasks such as channel estimation, jamming detection, or mitigation, rather than addressing them jointly. To overcome these limitations, we propose a two-stage convolutional neural network (CNN)-based variational autoencoder (VAE) framework for joint channel estimation and jamming robustness. The proposed method refines the least square (LS) estimates while generalizing effectively across both jammed and unjammed conditions. Unlike conventional approaches, it achieves accurate and resilient channel estimation without explicit jamming detection or prior knowledge of the jammer. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework maintains robust performance under multi-tone jamming, achieving a bit error rate (BER) of 1% with only a 0.7 dB increase in Eb/N0compared to unjammed operation conditions.

title: Implementation of Spike-Timing-Dependent Plasticity for epileptic seizure recovery on neuromorphic memristive hardware.
abstract: Neuromorphic engineers have spent decades developing efficient, brain-inspired computing hardware. This field was significantly advanced by the emergence of nanoscale memristors, which emulate synaptic connections and enable insitu learning algorithms like Spike-Timing-Dependent Plasticity (STDP). However, the widespread application of current memristors is hindered by limited reliability, particularly their difficulty in stably storing analog resistive values. This limitation can be overcome by exploiting a binary-weight stochastic STDP learning rule that leverages the more reliable binary memory capability of memristors. In this work, we implement this stochastic binary STDP algorithm on a neuromorphic hardware platform intended for real-time processing of brain Local Field Potential (LFP) signals, allowing the system to sense epileptic activity and prevent seizures in a closed-loop setup. Using synthetic signals generated by a hippocampal loop model, we demonstrate that a memristive crossbar can use STDP to learn neural correlations to detect and eventually prevent seizures. This outcome serves as a proof of concept for implanting a neuromorphic chip to inhibit epileptic seizures in the brain.

title: A 40 μW 8-bit Accelerator Wake-Up Circuit for Always-on Smart IoT Sensor Monitoring.
abstract: IoT sensors and devices rely heavily on cloud-based processing, especially in healthcare monitoring, for sensor data analysis, incurring high data transfer costs and energy consumption. To reduce constant data transmission, always-on smart sensors can use lightweight brain-inspired Hyperdimensional computing (HDC) models to efficiently classify sensor data that requires further resource-intensive cloud processing. We propose an all-digital CMOS always-on smart sensor accelerator for energy-constrained smart sensing applications. The proposed wake-up circuit architecture maintains HDC inference accuracy with INT-8 precision for complex datasets, where 1-bit quantization is not feasible. We introduce a novel systolic similarity search unit that utilizes a small systolic array to calculate hypervector cosine similarity metrics, and an energy-efficient near-memory fused item memory + multiply-accumulate systolic array encoder. This work achieves extremely low power consumption of 39.21-92.59 μW in typical applications, consuming only 120.01 nJ/inference.

title: An IZO-Based 2T0C Compute-in-Memory Array with Adaptive Read Voltage Boosting for Energy-Efficient Edge AI.
abstract: Oxide-semiconductor (OS) thin-film transistor (TFT)-based 2T0C eDRAM cells are promising for energy-efficient compute-in-memory (CIM) owing to their ultra-low leakage, high ION/IOFFratio, and long data retention. However, conventional OS devices suffer from low drive current and threshold-voltage (VTH) shift, leading to high operating voltages and accuracy degradation in large-scale CIM arrays. In this work, we fabricate a 64×64 indium–zinc–oxide (IZO) TFT CIM array using a BEOL-compatible self-aligned top-gate (SATG) process. The array achieves sub-0.1 V analog computation with data retention exceeding 120 s. To address VTHshift, an adaptive read-voltage boosting (ARVB) scheme is proposed, which expands the CIM operating window by 5.63× and improves VGG-16 inference accuracy to 92.15%. A PCB-based evaluation platform is developed for chip-level evaluation. The fabricated IZO CIM array achieves a peak energy efficiency of 34.75 TOPS/W@8bIN8bW, demonstrating the strong potential of IZO-based CIM for low-power AI deployment.

title: PathDiff: Efficient Patch-Level Histology Image Synthesis with Pathology-Prior Guided Diffusion.
abstract: To address the challenge of data scarcity and high computational cost in digital pathology, we introduce PathDiff. It is an efficient adaptation framework for diffusion-based patch-level image synthesis that, for the first time, explicitly integrates pathology-specific priors to ensure diagnostic fidelity. Unlike existing approaches that require large-scale datasets or heavy computation, PathDiff combines LoRA, Textual Inversion, and a Q-Former within a pathology-guided denoising process, which emphasizes diagnostically critical regions such as nuclei and glandular structures. This design enables faithful and diverse patch generation with only limited training data and modest resources. Extensive experiments on PCam and TCGA-BRCA demonstrate that PathDiff consistently outperforms representative GAN-and diffusion-based baselines in both visual fidelity and semantic alignment, while achieving comparable classification improvements to foundation-scale models at a fraction of the cost. These results highlight PathDiff as a practical and domain-aware solution for data augmentation in computational pathology.

title: Quantum Circuit Pruning: Improving Fidelity via Compilation-Aware Circuit Approximation.
abstract: This work presents a routing-aware pruning strategy for quantum circuits executed on Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices. We propose a method to remove parametric controlled rotations whose small rotation angles do not justify the routing overhead required for their implementation. By selectively pruning such gates, the method mitigates fidelity loss arising from additional SWAP operations introduced during compilation. Our approach evaluates whether executing a gate leads to greater fidelity loss than omitting it. Simulations on benchmark circuits with realistic noise models show that the method reduces two-qubit gate counts (up to 48.6%) while improving final state fidelity (up to 47.7%), especially for larger circuits where routing costs dominate.

title: A Low-Power CMOS-Spintronic Neuromorphic Network Based on Vortex Oscillators.
abstract: This paper presents a low-power CMOS interface for magnetic tunnel junction-based vortex oscillator (MTJ-VO) devices, suitable for neuromorphic networks. In the proposed approach, a rectified linear unit (ReLU)-like function is implemented by exploiting the dependence of the MTJ-VO frequency on its bias current (MTJ-ReLU). Compared with prior works, the proposed MTJ-VO-based neuron offers the distinct advantage of directly connecting multiple neurons to realize more complex neural networks. The CMOS interface was designed and verified through transistor-level simulations in a 65 nm CMOS technology using MTJ-VO data obtained from device measurements. Finally, the functionality of the MTJ-ReLU neuron was validated by implementing a 784×256×10 artificial neural network (ANN), achieving a test accuracy of 94%.

title: Phase-Change Memory Based Passive Timing Circuits for DRAM Refresh Management.
abstract: Timers play a crucial role in integrated circuit design. Cycle-based stamp counters are commonly used in various applications, such as CPU timing management and DRAM refresh operations. However, precise counting with digital counters comes with significant overhead. We propose a novel Phase-Change Memory (PCM) based passive timer for efficient timing. The passive and spontaneous conductance drift effect of PCM makes the timer highly energy-efficient. Through experiments using measured PCM conductance drift data, we compare our proposed PCM-based passive timer with traditional timers implemented in CMOS circuits. Our design achieves 121× better area efficiency and 8125.7× higher power efficiency compared to previous solutions. In the context of DRAM refresh management, the proposed solution requires only 0.1% area overhead and 0.14% power overhead, showcasing its practicality and efficiency.

title: A Static-Gradient, IC-Based 0.5-T NMR Spectrometer for 2D Diffusion-Relaxation Analysis of Solid Peanuts.
abstract: We present a compact, IC-based low-field NMR spectrometer that achieves diffusion-sensitive measurements without bulky gradient hardware, by using the inherent static magnetic gradient of a 0.5-T Halbach magnet. A custom 180-nm CMOS NMR ASIC integrates an arbitrary pulse sequencer, an RF transmitter, and a low-noise receiver within a die area of 5 mm2, enabling fully portable operation. Using the static gradient (gavg= 0.5 T/m), we demonstrate two-dimensional (2D) diffusion–relaxation (D–T2) experiments on solid peanuts during drying at 60°C. These measurements reveal oil molecular mobility and moisture loss without oil extraction. The system maintains a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 29 dB and stable operation across off-center regions with strong static gradients. These results establish a chip-scale, gradient-electronics-free NMR platform that bridges integrated-circuit design and magnetic resonance sensing, enabling field-deployable, non-destructive analysis of agricultural, food, and biological materials.

title: An Ultra-Low-Power IR-UWB Energy-Harvesting Tag for Unsynchronized Multi-User Transmission.
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-low-power wireless tag for kHz-rate sensing in unsynchronized energy-harvesting wireless sensor networks (EHWSNs). The tag implements a multiuser time-hopping impulse-radio ultra-wideband (TH-IR-UWB)-based scheme that enables the simultaneous and unsynchronized operation of 64 tags transmitting asynchronously to a single base station. The SoC is fabricated in a low-cost 180-nm 1P6M CMOS process. It integrates a digital core, a packet generator, a pulse generator, a UWB transmitter, an XO-based clock generator, and a power management unit that includes an energy harvester for direct over-the-air powering or wireless battery charging. The proposed TH-IR-UWB uses packets of 255bits each, consisting of a preamble, data bits, and CRC at a transmit rate of 256Hz which can be increased to 4096Hz by reducing the payload length. A sequence set with bounded correlation is constructed through a systematic and exhaustive search to support reliable multi-user detection. Measurements confirm correct packet timing and an effective data rate of 57.34kbs-1per tag. At a 1-V supply, the pulse generator consumes 18.9µW on average, and the transmitter consumes 29µW during operation with −1dBm RF output power, occupying an area of 1.5mm2. The results demonstrate a scalable, energy-efficient telemetry platform suited for dense EHWSNs.

title: Robust Data-Driven Distributed Control Strategy for Dynamic Energy Scheduling in Hybrid Energy Systems.
abstract: This paper proposes a robust data-driven distributed control strategy for dynamic energy scheduling in hybrid energy storage systems (HESSs) comprising fuel cells (FCs) and lithium-ion batteries. The proposed framework integrates a robust recurrent deep network (R2DN)-based controller that enables fully distributed coordination among heterogeneous energy sources without relying on centralized communication. By embedding degradation indicators of FCs and virtual state-of-charge (SoC) variables of batteries into the control design, the strategy achieves adaptive power allocation among multiple FCs, SoC equalization of batteries, and fast DC-bus voltage regulation under dynamic operating conditions. The R2DN controller provides intrinsic stability guarantees through contraction and Lipschitz constraints, ensuring robustness against parameter variations and external disturbances. Simulation in MATLAB/SIMULINK verified the performance of proposed control method.

title: A 1-10.7GHz Low-Jitter 8-Phase Injection-Locked Clock Generator with Supply-Voltage Feedback in 28 nm CMOS.
abstract: With the advancements in high-speed integrated circuits, the demand for compact-area, high-performance multi-phase clock generation is increasing. This paper presents a small-area, low-jitter 8-phase injection-locked clock generator with supply-voltage feedback. The proposed delay-locked loop (DLL) employs a low-dropout regulator (LDO) to directly control the supply voltages of both the delay line and ring voltage-controlled oscillator (RVCO). This design effectively suppresses noise coupling into the RVCO and minimizes replica control-loop-induced mismatches, thereby achieving both an enhanced locking range and reduced output jitter. Fabricated in 28–nm CMOS process under 0.9–V supply, the design achieves an ultra-wideband locking range of 8-phase clock output spanning 1–10.7GHz. At 7 GHz, the measured jitter is 26 fs (integrated from 100 Hz to 1 GHz ), while occupying an area of less than 0.012 mm2. The compact area, high performance, and wide locking range make this solution highly suitable for integration with high-speed ADC and other mixed-signal systems requiring precise timing synchronization.

title: Detector-in-Memory for Massive MIMO Detection.
abstract: Massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) signal detection is essential for 6G and beyond. However, current detectors, both digital and in-memory computing (IMC)-based, suffer from high energy and latency overheads. We propose the Detector-in-Memory (DiM) architecture to overcome these challenges. DiM is an IMC-based architecture that employs symbol slicers instead of column ADCs, and an intrinsically complex-valued IMC bitcell (BC) to realize a high-dimensional complex-valued matrix-vector multiplication (C-MVM). The use of symbol slicers results in a 128× reduction in the number of quantizations per symbol, while the use of a 28T4C complex-valued IMC BC reduces the transistor count by 30% compared to real-valued BCs. Simulations in a commercial 28nm CMOS indicate that DiM achieves an 11× higher energy efficiency and 7× greater area efficiency than state-of-the-art MIMO detectors, while meeting the QPSK 3GPP error vector magnitude (EVM) specification of -15.15dB.

title: RISC-V and SHA-256 Accelerator Hackathon: A Problem-Based Learning Approach to Hardware-Software Co-Design.
abstract: Hackathons have emerged as a powerful Problem-Based Learning (PBL) approach in engineering education, fostering active engagement, teamwork, and problem-solving under real-world constraints. This paper presents an educational hackathon in which students designed a RISC-V core based on the Imagination University Program and a SHA-256 cryptographic accelerator, implemented on a Xilinx Nexys A7-100T FPGA board. The hackathon was integrated into a VLSI course with three preparatory workshops—focused on FPGA setup, accelerator interfacing, and software co-design—culminating in a final open-ended challenge. The goals of the hackathon were fourfold: (1) apply PBL in hardware/software co-design, (2) enhance practical FPGA and RISC-V skills, (3) develop collaboration and creativity under time constraints, and (4) increase motivation toward VLSI careers. Survey results revealed increased motivation, enhanced technical and collaborative skills, and strengthened career interest. This work demonstrates the value of hackathons as a PBL methodology for advancing practical skills and professional readiness in computer engineering education.

title: 3D Monolithic Integrated Indium Tin Oxide-Silicon Hybrid Leaky Integrate and Fire Neuron.
abstract: Neuromorphic circuits offer energy and area-efficient operation for edge applications. Being inspired by the massive connectivity of biological neural networks, these would also require dense connectivity that can be achieved by 3D integration. Conventional analog subthreshold neuron circuits are implemented in Si-CMOS technology and require a capacitor to integrate the incoming synaptic inputs, which tend to occupy a larger area. In this paper, we demonstrate a Leaky Integrate and Fire (LIF) neuron in Amorphous Oxide Semiconductor (AOS) technology using Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) channel nFET. By exploiting its low off-state leakage in a 2T gain-cell integrator that allows long charge retention, we show a capacitor-less circuit. We propose an ITO-nFET neuron circuit and also a 3D hybrid neuron circuit that combines Si-pFET along with ITO-nFET, which can be potentially fabricated in a Monolithic 3D IC technology to reduce overall footprint. The circuits are demonstrated based on a compact model calibrated to experimental ITO-nFET data. The proposed ITO-nFET neuron circuit is designed with 65nm technology design rules and consumes an energy of 12.95pJ/spike at a supply voltage of 1.2V with a spiking frequency of 166.66kHz and utilizes 96.7µm2area. The hybrid circuit is shown to operate at much reduced energy of 9.58pJ/spike at a spiking frequency of 125kHz for the same conditions. Furthermore, our neurons are evaluated in a convolutional spiking neural network (CSNN) and demonstrate a high inference accuracy of >97% on the N-MNIST dataset.

title: Design and validation of a clocked gm-C bandpower extraction circuit for biosignal analysis.
abstract: This paper presents a compact and hardware-efficient bandpower extraction circuit for analog spectral analysis of local field potentials (LFPs), enabling robust real-time biomarker detection for closed-loop deep brain stimulation (DBS). A clocked-transconductor architecture provides digitally tuneable low-frequency filtering with minimal capacitance and a fixed bias current, followed by a cross-coupled full-wave rectifier for highly power-efficient envelope detection. The circuit is designed and simulated in a 65 nm CMOS process and cross-validated using off-the-shelf components in a board-level implementation, enabling realistic in vitro emulation prior to silicon fabrication. The prototype achieves a tuneable centre frequency of 4 to 33 Hz, a quality factor of 0.7 to 9.4, and fine frequency steps down to 1%, meeting the requirements of neural biomarkers used clinically in closed-loop neuromodulation.

title: Approximate Reciprocal-based Divider.
abstract: Recent years have seen a growing demand for smart, portable, and high-speed processing systems, posing significant challenges for digital circuit design in terms of power consumption, silicon area, and latency. Approximate Computing (AC) has emerged as an effective approach to address these challenges by allowing controlled computational errors in error-tolerant applications. In this paper, a novel approximate divider architecture based on a reciprocal algorithm is proposed. The proposed design achieves improvements of 86% in area, 92% in delay, and 79% in power consumption compared with an exact divider. The accuracy of the proposed divider is evaluated in image and signal processing applications. For change detection, it achieves a Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) of 0.99 and a Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) of 55 dB, compared with average values of 0.97 and 47.5 dB in state-of-the-art designs. In foreground extraction, the average SSIM and PSNR are 0.96 and 37.54 dB, respectively. For heartbeat QRS detection using the Pan–Tompkins algorithm, the proposed divider achieves a PSNR of 60 dB, demonstrating its suitability for error-resilient applications.

title: The Hacker Fab: An Open-Source Initiative for Nanofabrication Education.
abstract: Teaching nanofabrication to undergraduates can be challenging due to the limited availability and high cost of processing equipment and infrastructure, such as cleanroom facilities. The Hacker Fab, an initiative launched in 2023 at Carnegie Mellon University, seeks to lower these barriers by developing innovative, low-cost, open-source semiconductor fabrication tools and processes. The initiative breaks traditional models by introducing students to the fundamental principles of semiconductor device fabrication in an affordable and accessible manner through a project-based course that provides opportunities to engage in hands-on projects that directly contribute to the advancement of the laboratory infrastructure. The unique, scalable model is also highly adaptable, enabling the ability to follow industry and research trends.

title: Design and Validation of a Wireless System for Bokashi Compost Monitoring.
abstract: Bokashi composting is an anaerobic fermentation process that offers a sustainable alternative for organic waste management by preserving nutrients and reducing gaseous emissions associated with aerobic composting. However, the lack of practical and energy-efficient monitoring tools limits its optimization and broader adoption under real-world conditions. This paper presents a low-power, LoRa-enabled IoT platform designed for autonomous, real-time monitoring of Bokashi fermentation processes. The proposed system demonstrates the feasibility of long-range, ultra-low-power wireless sensing to observe anaerobic fermentation dynamics while operating under constrained energy resources. Experimental operation shows that the platform can achieve 38 hours of standalone autonomy on a compact Li-ion battery. An on-board solar panel can further extend this autonomy based on solar radiation levels. Overall, this work highlights the potential of low-power LoRa-based IoT architectures to support climate-smart agricultural practises and sustainable waste management through real-time monitoring of anaerobic bio-processes.

title: A 442.42 TOPS/W RRAM-based Digital Computing-in-Memory Accelerator for BF16×1-bit Vision Transformer.
abstract: RRAM-based Computing-in-Memory (CIM) architectures are promising for efficient Transformer inference, yet analog approaches suffer from circuit non-idealities and limited precision, leading to accuracy degradation. In this paper, a fully digital CIM accelerator based on RRAM is proposed to achieve a better trade-off between accuracy, energy, and area. Then, a fully digital RRAM-based CIM accelerator is designed with an area-efficient 4T-XOR and a fine-grained mantissa shifter. Implemented on 28nm technology node, the proposed design achieves a peak normalized energy efficiency of 442.42 TOPS/W.

title: Balancing Speed and Accuracy for Robust Analog-Mixed Signal Circuit Design using Closed-Loop Reinforcement Learning with Ensemble Neural Network Surrogates.
abstract: Analog/mixed-signal (AMS) circuit sizing requires exploring high-dimensional, constrained design spaces under expensive SPICE simulations, while maintaining robustness to out-of-distribution (OOD) parameter proposals. We propose a fidelity-aware reinforcement learning framework (RL-PPO-Online) that unifies (i) SPICE-in-the-loop verification and (ii) ensemble neural network guided regularization for surrogate-assisted optimization. Another PPO policy (RL-PPO-Offline) is trained using an ensemble neural network for fast performance prediction, while a discriminator penalizes OOD actions to stabilize surrogate-only updates. We further introduce RL-PPO-Blend, which schedules a small fraction of SPICE queries (0.2–5%) on top of RL-PPO-Offline to provide a tunable speed–fidelity trade-off. On challenging ADC front-end sizing tasks in 28 nm (bootstrapped sampling switch and input buffer + switch), the proposed method improves pass rates over DDPG and LLM baselines, and achieves near-online accuracy with substantially reduced simulation cost.

title: LUT-SNN: Efficient Spiking Neural Networks with Fast Parallel Inference.
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) have shown great potential for low-power intelligent sensing and edge computing due to their sparse and event-driven nature. However, inference in conventional Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) models requires sequential membrane potential updates across time steps, hindering parallel execution. To overcome this limitation, we propose a lookup-table-based parallel LIF neuron model (LUT-SNN) and an algorithm–hardware co-optimization framework for acceleration. For the algorithm, by precomputing threshold boundaries, the temporal recurrence is transformed into a spatial lookup operation, achieving constant-time parallel inference. Based on this model, we design a systolic-array accelerator that employs comparator trees and on-chip LUT modules for efficient neuronal computation. Experimental results show that, compared with standard LIF-based SNNs, LUT-SNN achieves up to 2.89× speedup on the proposed accelerator for ResNet-18 model on TinyImageNet datasets with 4 timesteps, while maintaining comparable accuracy. This work provides a new perspective for efficient and parallel SNN inference and hardware implementation.

title: Performance Pragma-Based Design Space Pruning and Exploration for High-Level Synthesis.
abstract: High-level synthesis (HLS) tools are widely used to design field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) and application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) using high-level languages like C/C++. Existing tools typically provide a set of directives for optimizing generated designs, necessitating exploration of the vast design space formed by directive combinations to obtain satisfactory designs. To tackle this, numerous HLS design space exploration (DSE) frameworks have been proposed in recent years. However, these frameworks either inadequately prune the design space or lack pruning method, leading to excessively long exploration time. This work replaces traditional pragma combinations with the newly released PERFORMANCE pragma in Vitis HLS. Our approach eliminates unreasonable pragma combinations and substantially reduces the total number of pragmas employed. It also prunes pragma parameter values to exclude redundant designs, thereby further shrinking the design space. The proposed framework employs graph neural networks (GNNs) to predict the quality of results (QoR) of candidate designs and adopts Bayesian optimization (BO) for efficient exploration. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves a Pareto front comparable to the state-of-the-art (SOTA) with a 38.30% improvement in ADRS.

title: A 16-Channel Rapid On-Chip Seizure Classifier With Online Re-Training for Closed-loop Neuromodulation.
abstract: Closed-loop neuromodulation-based deep-brain stimulation devices are increasingly used for treating neurological disorders such as epilepsy. These systems require on-chip intelligence for reliable seizure onset detection under strict power and area constraints. Achieving low-latency detection while adapting to the dynamic nature of neural signals remains a major challenge. This paper presents an on-chip seizure detection framework based on online re-training. The proposed system continuously adapts to variations in neural recordings through a two-step self-labelling and balancing mechanism that ensures stable and unbiased model updates. A logistic regression classifier enables efficient real-time inference, and a stochastic gradient descent-based balanced re-training engine enables adaptation over time. The 16-channel prototype achieves a sensitivity of 95.3%, specificity of 95.2%, a rapid inference time of only 240 ms, an energy efficiency of 1.83 nJ/classification and a compact area of 0.017 mm2.

title: A Near-Sensor Image Compression Architecture with RRAM-based Hyperdimensional Encoder for Smart Vision.
abstract: Image compression is crucial for edge vision systems, but traditional human vision-optimized methods are inefficient for machine tasks and raw data transmission faces bandwidth constraints. To tackle these issues, this paper exploits the compatibility between brain-inspired hyperdimensional computing (HDC) and in-memory computing, proposing an RRAM-based HDC architecture for near-sensor image compression. This architecture encodes images into high-dimensional vectors near sensor, enabling direct feature extraction and compression for downstream tasks on a host processor. The proposed method achieves a bitrate of 0.361 bpp, improving compression efficiency by 39.8% compared to existing machine vision compression approaches. Benefiting from the parallel computing capability of the RRAM-based in-memory architecture, the system enables highly energy-efficient implementation of HDC. Simulated using the 28 nm CMOS process at 100MHz, the system consumes 5.44 mW, representing a 9.4× power reduction over ASIC systems. The proposed all-in-memory encoding module achieves a system latency of 3.53 ms, which is 202× lower than the multi-cycle approach.

title: A Low Noise Active Pixel Circuit Using Dual Correlated Double Sampling for Dynamic TFT Integrated X-Ray Imaging.
abstract: Active pixel sensors (APS) based on thin-film transistors (TFTs) show great potential for low-dose and high–signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) X-ray imaging. However, a considerable amount of pre-amplification reset noise is a major concern. In this work, a novel 4T-2C APS circuit implementing a dual correlated double sampling (D-CDS) technique is proposed, which can simultaneously suppress pre-amplification reset noise and post-amplification low-frequency flicker noise. The current-integration readout mode provides a low-pass filtering effect, effectively reducing the thermal noise caused by the conduction of the reset transistor. The APS circuit implemented with oxide TFTs achieves a charge-to-current conversion gain of 7.28 μA/pC and a nonlinearity of 0.42%. Compared with the conventional CDS-based 3T-1C pixel, the proposed circuit reduces the pre-amplification noise by 46.7%, demonstrating its suitability for low-dose, high-SNR dynamic X-ray medical imaging.

title: GreenMorph: Sustainable Neuromorphic Computing through Energy-Harvesting and Energy-Driven Online STDP Learning.
abstract: In recent years, the rapidly increasing computational demands of artificial intelligence (AI) have underscored the need for more sustainable and energy-efficient computing solutions. This paper introduces GreenMorph - a carbon-aware Spiking Neural Network (SNN) framework that relies on energy harvesting and can be driven by the energy level. GreenMorph dynamically adjusts timesteps and employs similarity-based neuron pruning to optimize energy consumption to achieve carbon neutrality during operation. Experimental evaluations on benchmark datasets show that timestep adaptation reduces training energy by 15.15% without accuracy degradation, while combining timestep adaptation with neuron pruning achieves an 88.10% reduction in training energy at the cost of only 3.01% accuracy loss. During inference, similarity-based neuron pruning reduces computation energy by 27.18% with just 0.35% accuracy loss, and by up to 88.32% with 8.81% accuracy loss.

title: Electronic-Photonic Hybrid CIM-based Ising Machine with Interaction-Aware Update Strategy for Combinatorial Optimization Problems.
abstract: Ising machines present a promising solution for tackling NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems (COPs). While Compute-in-Memory (CIM) architectures enhance performance by minimizing data movement and enabling efficient multiply-and-accumulate (MAC) operations, their scalability is hindered by IR-drop issues, and their speed is limited by the sequential nature of simulated annealing (SA). This work introduces an electronic–photonic hybrid CIM Ising machine to address these limitations. The design leverages discharge based 4-bit FeFET compute cells to reduce power consumption and optical bitlines to perform lossless summation through phase modulation, thereby eliminating IR-drop. An interaction-aware update (IAU) strategy is further proposed to enable parallel spin updates. Evaluated on a 1024-node Max-Cut problem and a 29-city TSP under a fully connected Ising model, the design achieves 99% and 98% of the theoretical optima, respectively. Compared to baseline implementations, our work delivers >26 × speedup and a >1.5× improvement in figure-of-merits which reflects the capability and energy consumption of Ising machine.

title: Debiasing Diffusion Model: Enhancing Fairness through Latent Representation Learning in Stable Diffusion Model.
abstract: Diffusion-based models excel at synthesizing realistic images but often inherit and amplify societal biases from their training data, leading to unfair group representations. Existing debiasing methods typically rely on predefined sensitive attributes, external classifiers, or large language models, which limits their applicability to complex, continuous demographic variations. To overcome these limitations, we propose the Debiasing Diffusion Model (DDM), a novel framework that fine-tunes a Stable Diffusion Model to learn fair latent representations. DDM integrates a temporary indicator module during training, which guides the model to become invariant to sensitive attributes without requiring explicit attribute labels at inference time. This approach not only ensures a balanced distribution for neutral prompts but also minimizes performance disparities when attributes are specified. We demonstrate the effectiveness of DDM through comprehensive experiments, showcasing its ability to enhance fairness beyond the scope of conventional techniques.

title: S2PUF: A <1.77E-8 BER Schmitt Effect SRAM PUF with Load Tilt Masking for Resource-Constrained systems.
abstract: Physical unclonable functions (PUFs) have emerged as a promising solution for resource-constrained key generation and authentication. However, PUFs are highly sensitive to voltage and temperature variations, making it difficult to achieve 100% reliability throughout their entire lifecycle. Existing solutions often require large overhead in terms of masking or error correction codes (ECC) to ensure reliability. This work proposes S2PUF, a schmitt effect SRAM PUF that successfully eliminates all unreliable bits without the need for expensive temperature sweeps. By using an all-NMOS structure and leveraging hysteresis to achieves both high native reliability and low power. Additionally, a load tilt masking technique is employed to precisely adjust controllable loads for identifying unreliable bits, further enhancing PUF reliability to ~100%. The S2PUF is fabricated in 180-nm standard CMOS and achieves "0" bit error rate (BER) (BERpes, <1.77E−8) by masking 8.52% of PUF bits. It also shows 0.391%/10 ℃ and 0.398%/0.1 V native bit error across temperature variations of −40 ℃ to 120 ℃ and voltage variations from 0.6 V to 2.0 V. The core energy per bit at 0.6 V is 12.56 fJ.

title: Live Demonstration: Hardware-Bound IP Protection for OWL-ViT on Edge Devices.
abstract: We demonstrate a hardware-bound Intellectual Property (IP) protection scheme for transformer models on edge devices. Our method binds the OWL-ViT [1], an open-vocabulary object detection model, to specific hardware using a Physical Unclonable Function (PUF). The model weights are reversibly obfuscated using PUF-derived cryptographic keys, catastrophically degrading the performance of unauthorized devices and thus preventing IP theft. The proposed method incurs only a moderate inference overhead on the authorized target for real time applications.

title: A Passive-LoRa Tag Chip Achieving 78m Battery-Free Bidirectional Communication with Standard LoRa Devices.
abstract: The massive deployment of the next-generation Internet of Things (IoT) requires node chips with ultra-low power consumption, low cost, protocol compatibility, and long-range communication. Although the recent passive-BLE/Wi-Fi tags based on wireless power harvesting and backscattering communication present a potential solution, their limited communication range remains a major bottleneck. To address this challenge, this paper presents a crystal-less passive-LoRa tag that achieves battery-free bidirectional communication with standard LoRa devices: 1) A LoRa-shaping backscattering technique based on beat-frequency wireless clock recovery is proposed, enabling the battery-free uplink signal to be received by standard LoRa devices. 2) A beat-splitting self-downconversion technique is proposed to enable the battery-free tag to demodulate standard LoRa signals. The proposed techniques are implemented into a passive-LoRa chip fabricated in a 65nm CMOS process. Measured results show that the chip achieves battery-free bidirectional LoRa communication with an equivalent range up to 78m.

title: Energy-Efficient Compute-in-Memory Macro for BNNs in Edge AI using NV-SRAM.
abstract: In this paper, an area and energy efficient in-memory binary neural network (BNN) accelerator is proposed by employing the CMOS-compatible non-volatile (NV) SRAM. The developed NV-SRAM provides the on-chip non-volatile storage for weights and feature maps without off-chip reload, achieving robust data retention and mitigating information leakage. The proposed NV-SRAM design utilizes less transistors and lower operating voltage 800 mV as compared with the existing nonvolatile SRAM with tunneling effect. In a case study to support binarized 20×20 MNIST image processing, a (400×200) SRAM array is designed to efficiently map for the 400-bit feature data using dedicated peripheral circuits. The chip design has been implemented in GlobalFoundries 22 nm FDSOI technology and verified by Monte Carlo analysis. Results show very high energy efficiency of 5 fJ per logic operation with around 20% area saving as compared to the state-of-the-art. It also demonstrates the suitability of such an accelerator for edge AI applications with low-power by holding the inference accuracy which reaches 94.78% on MNIST dataset.

title: FPGA-Based Spiking Neural Network AutoEncoders for Real-Time Anomaly Detection in LHC Physics.
abstract: Real-time anomaly detection at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) requires ultra-low-latency inference under strict computational constraints. This paper presents the FPGA implementation of Spiking Neural Network AutoEncoders (SNN-AEs) for anomaly detection at the trigger level. Multiple SNN-AE architectures are synthesized on Xilinx UltraScale+ FPGAs and their resource utilization is characterized. Event-based spike processing reduces DSP usage by 67% and LUT usage by 53% compared to conventional Deep NN implementations while maintaining Area Under Curve (AUC) = 0.899 for charged Higgs-like scalar (h+) detection. The smallest SNN-AE architecture consumes only 1.99% LUTs and 1.94% DSPs, enabling viable integration into existing L1 trigger systems. Using the Compact Muon Solenoid (CMS) ADC2021 dataset, hardware resource comparisons are provided with FPGA-deployed DNN AutoEncoders across multiple signal models and architectural configurations.

title: SEGA-PointNet: A Semantic Enhancement and Global Aggregation Network for Maize Organ Segmentation from 3D Point Clouds.
abstract: Accurate segmentation of crop organs from three-dimensional (3D) point clouds is critical for intelligent perception in precision agriculture. Existing point cloud networks have limited ability to jointly capture local geometric features and global semantic structures. To address this limitation, this study proposes SEGA-PointNet (Semantic Enhancement and Global Aggregation PointNet), an improved architecture built upon PointNet++. SEGA-PointNet integrates three core modules: SPSA (Semantic-Perceptual Spatial Attention) for multi-scale spatial enhancement, KAN (Kolmogorov-Arnold Network) for nonlinear feature modeling, and GLSFA (Global-Local Semantic Feature Aggregation) for semantic fusion across scales. Experiments on the syau_single_maize dataset demonstrate that SEGA-PointNet achieves higher overall accuracy and mean intersection over union compared with existing point cloud models. Ablation studies verify the positive contribution of each module. SEGA-PointNet provides an effective and extensible framework for 3D semantic segmentation of complex crop structures.

title: LSMC Meets GPU Acceleration: Scalable and High-Quality Multi-Row Detailed Placement.
abstract: Detailed placement is a crucial stage in VLSI physical design, optimizing wirelength, timing, routability and power under complex constraints such as edge spacing, site alignment and fence regions. With the aggressive increase of design utilization and adoption of multi-row height cells in advanced technology nodes, existing detailed placers struggle with efficiency and quality, often becoming trapped in local minima. In this work, we develop GPU-DPO, a fast and high-quality GPU-accelerated detailed placement framework built on top of the OpenROAD infrastructure, which leverages Large-Step Markov Chain techniques to escape local optima and improve placement quality. GPU-DPO is the first GPU-accelerated detailed placer with the capability of fully supporting movable and reorderable multi-row height cells. Experimental results on testcases with varying utilization demonstrate that, in comparison with DPO [42] (the default detailed placer in OpenROAD) and ABCDPlace [27] (the state-of-the-art GPU-accelerated detailed placer), our approach achieves an average reduction of post-detailed placement half-perimeter wirelength (HPWL) by 1.71% and 3.5% respectively, while consuming similar runtime as ABCDPlace.

title: A High-Performance and Area-Efficient Unified Butterfly Module for ML-KEM Polynomial Computations.
abstract: With the rapid advancement of quantum computing technology, traditional public-key cryptographic algorithms are gradually losing their security guarantees. To address this challenge, the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) announced the Module Lattice-based Key Encapsulation Mechanism (ML-KEM) in 2022, whose security is based on the computational hardness of the Module Learning with Errors (MLWE) problem. This makes it resistant to quantum attacks in the foreseeable future. In this paper, we propose a high-performance and area-efficient butterfly computation unit that supports various polynomial operations in ML-KEM, including the Number Theoretic Transform (NTT), Inverse NTT (INTT), and Point-wise Multiplication (PWM). The proposed butterfly unit is constructed from basic modular arithmetic submodules and incorporates a rescheduled Karatsuba algorithm to enhance the efficiency of polynomial multiplication without incurring significant hardware overhead.

title: Circuit Similarity Based Initial Parameter Sampling for Tool Parameter Exploration.
abstract: Tool parameters in logic synthesis and physical design tools significantly affect the design implementation and ultimately determine the quality of the resulting design. Each circuit has its own optimal set of tool parameters to achieve the best design quality, and various global optimization methods, such as Bayesian optimization, genetic algorithms, and reinforcement learning, are commonly employed to find them. However, these methods often require long runtimes to explore numerous parameter combinations. In this paper, we accelerate the optimization process by leveraging pre-optimized tool parameter sets from other circuits, under the assumption that circuits with similar designs exhibit comparable optimal tool parameter configurations. Experimental results show that the proposed method consistently outperforms conventional approaches, achieving an average of 14.3% greater improvement in energy–delay product within the same runtime, and requiring 2.8× smaller runtime to reach the same level of improvement.

title: A16K: 1.6nm NSFET, FSFET, and CFET Technology Libraries for Chip-Level VLSI Prediction.
abstract: Semiconductor process is evolving more than ever before. Major foundries plan to mass-produce the 2nm process, while academia continues to announce devices for even more advanced nodes. Despite the continuous scaling in technology nodes, it remains uncertain to what extent digital VLSI can further improve in advanced and future nodes. Therefore, we present A16K: the first public 16 Angstrom (Å) technology library and report the following results. 1) It is crucial to design standard cells with fewer tracks compared to the 2nm library for better PPA (power, performance, and area) improvement. 2) Increasing usable signal tracks by adopting Buried Power Rail (BPR) guarantees substantial PPA improvement. 3) 3T CFET library shows -35.5% power, -44.1% area, and +2.84% effective frequency enhancement compared to the 2nm counterpart. Based on these results, we emphasize that design technology co-optimization (DTCO) is essential for process development in addition to native transistor scaling.

title: An Isomorphic Transformation for Hardware Implemented Non-negative Neural Networks.
abstract: High speed and efficient accelerators such as neuromorphic photonics are becoming increasingly popular, as they can significantly improve the computation speed and energy efficiency of matrix-based calculations, leading to femtojoule per MAC efficiency. However, deploying existing DL models on such platforms is not trivial, as a wide range of photonic neural network (PNN) architectures relies on incoherent setups and power-adding operational schemes that cannot natively represent negative quantities. This results in additional hardware complexity that increases costs and reduces energy efficiency. To overcome this, we can train non-negative neural networks and potentially exploit the full range of incoherent neuromorphic photonic capabilities. However, the existing non-negative training approaches cannot achieve the same level of accuracy as their regular counterparts. To this end, we introduce a methodology to obtain the non-negative isomorphic equivalents of regular artificial neural networks (ANNs) that meet the requirements of neuromorphic hardware, as it allows one to perform inference with non-negative-only parameters.

title: Open and Accessible Workflows for the education and Prototyping of Nanoelectronic Devices.
abstract: Modern semiconductor design is organised into a layered hierarchy of abstraction that governs the progression from device-level modelling to complete system realisation. This paper examines the methods and software tools used at each stage, spanning technology computer-aided design for device simulation, through mixed-signal and circuit-level verification, and culminating in FPGA prototyping and ASIC implementation. It places particular emphasis on the rising role of open-source electronic design automation ecosystems, which are increasingly complementing or displacing conventional proprietary solutions. The study shows how such tools enable educational and research institutions to undertake end-to-end semiconductor design using transparent, reproducible workflows. Open PDks, cloud-hosted automation frameworks, and shared community fabrication shuttles reduce cost and complexity, making silicon prototyping more accessible for students and investigators. Together, these innovations foster the democratisation of nanoelectronic and VLSI design by supporting open, interoperable processes that connect theoretical work, experimental validation, and physical fabrication.
