title: Multi-Source Localization in High-Noise Mixed Fields: A Logarithmic Spacing Multi-Concentric Circular Array and Conical Gridding Method.
abstract: In industrial production and maintenance, Sound Source Localization is a common method for monitoring and rapidly identifying fault points such as gas leaks and bearing damage. With the proliferation of embedded hardware supporting efficient matrix operations, methods based on Time Difference of Arrival (TDOA) for spatial reconstruction are gradually being replaced by those utilizing steering vectors derived from wave propagation models in irrotational fluids. Steering vector-based methods are often more sensitive to array geometry, which has led to the development of improved arrays based on compressed sensing theory, such as the logarithmic spiral array. However, in our practical evaluations, the logarithmic spiral array demonstrated poor performance in localizing far-field sources within hybrid near-field and far-field scenarios under high noise and struggled with designing effective spatial filters for low-frequency imaging tasks prone to high sidelobe contamination. To address these issues, we propose a modified multi-concentric circular array with logarithmic spacing and equal angular rotation, inspired by the design principles of the logarithmic spiral array. Concurrently, we introduce a non-uniform conical gridding method tailored to this array's characteristics to better facilitate spatial filtering. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed array design achieves superior performance in terms of sidelobe reduction, on-grid error, and off-grid error compared to the logarithmic spiral array in FISTA-based sparse reconstruction tasks involving high white noise and mixed-field sources. Furthermore, the proposed gridding method significantly outperforms traditional gridding techniques in sidelobe level, on-grid and off-grid errors, and computational cost.

title: Implementation and Evaluation of a Cryogenic DSP in 22-nm with Floating-Point Arithmetic for Estimating Qubit States.
abstract: Recent advancements in quantum computing have emphasized the need for scalable quantum–classical interfaces (QC-IFs) capable of controlling a huge number of qubits efficiently. Conventional QC-IFs, implemented at room temperature, face wiring and thermal challenges that limit system scalability as the number of qubits increases. To address these issues, we propose a cryogenic digital signal processor (DSP) architecture capable of performing qubit readout and control operations inside the dilution refrigerator. We implemented the DSP which replaced wide fixed-point operations by floating-point ones in a previous study. An ASIC was fabricated using a 22-nm CMOS bulk process. Compared with the previous study, power consumption and area increased at room temperature due to additional circuits. We conducted a leakage power analysis on this design based on transistor leakage characteristics at 25 °C and −73 °C. The results demonstrated a reduction of 96.6% compared to leakage power at 25 °C. These results demonstrate the feasibility of low-power, compact control electronics for future Cryo-CMOS control SoCs and fault-tolerant quantum computing systems.

title: From RTL to Prompt Coding: Empowering the Next Generation of Chip Designers through LLMs.
abstract: This paper presents an LLM-based learning platform for chip design education, aiming to make chip design accessible to beginners without overwhelming them with technical complexity. It represents the first educational platform that assists learners holistically across both frontend and backend design. The proposed approach integrates an LLM-based chat agent into a browser-based workflow built upon the Tiny Tapeout ecosystem. The workflow guides users from an initial design idea through RTL code generation to a tapeout-ready chip. To evaluate the concept, a case study was conducted with 18 high-school students. Within a 90-minute session they developed eight functional VGA chip designs in a 130 nm technology. Despite having no prior experience in chip design, all groups successfully implemented tapeout-ready projects. The results demonstrate the feasibility and educational impact of LLM-assisted chip design, highlighting its potential to attract and inspire early learners and significantly broaden the target audience for the field.

title: BrainRead: Multi-Sensor Earable System for Continuous Physiological Sensing.
abstract: We present BrainRead, a multimodal earable system designed for continuous physiological sensing through an integrated architecture spanning signal acquisition, on-device storage and processing, and wireless communication. The platform incorporates EarEEG, EarECG, EarPPG, a 6-axis IMU, and a IR temperature sensor within earbuds, supported by a modular neckband and chestbud subsystem housing dual MCUs, power management, storage, audio interfaces, and a BLE communication module. Hardware and functional validation confirms reliable neural, cardiac, and vascular signal acquisition, including alpha attenuation response during eyes-open or closed conditions and consistent ECG and PPG morphology. These results establish BrainRead as a versatile platform for continuous, multimodal physiological assessment, suitable for non-clinical tracking with potential applications in clinical settings and research.

title: A 16-nm 24.8 Mbps/mJ Utilization-Aware Dynamic Allocation Read Mapping Accelerator for Next-Generation Sequencing.
abstract: This paper presents the first utilization-aware dynamic allocation accelerator for short-read mapping in next-generation sequencing. The BITAP algorithm is employed and optimized to reduce computational complexity while deriving both edit distance and the actual mismatch pattern of the sequence alignment. The proposed architecture integrates a Dynamic BITAP Engine that achieves 95.3% utilization through horizontal and vertical dynamic allocation. Dual-Base Alignment and Exact-Match Detection are incorporated to minimize redundant operations. A novel Banded Backward Searching scheme tailored for the BITAP algorithm further reduces on-chip SRAM usage by 85% through shared state-vector reconstruction with banded scheme. Designed in TSMC 16-nm, the accelerator occupies 0.48 mm2, operates at 526 MHz, and consumes 162 mW, delivering 4.02 Gbps/s throughput and 24.8 Mbps/mJ energy efficiency. It achieves 8.65× area efficiency and 14.33× energy efficiency improvements over state-of-the-art designs while maintaining 99.7% accuracy compared with BWA-MEM. The results demonstrate a scalable and energy-efficient architecture for real-time portable data analysis for genome sequencing.

title: CLOAQ: Combined Logic and Angle Obfuscation for Quantum Circuits.
abstract: In the realm of quantum computing, quantum circuits serve as essential depictions of quantum algorithms, which are then compiled into executable operations for quantum computations. Quantum compilers are responsible for converting these algorithmic quantum circuits into versions compatible with specific quantum hardware, thus connecting quantum software with hardware. Nevertheless, untrusted quantum compilers present notable threats. They have the potential to result in the theft of quantum circuit designs and jeopardize sensitive intellectual property (IP). In this work, we propose CLOAQ, a quantum circuit obfuscation (QCO) approach that hides the logic and the phase angles of selected gates within the obfuscated quantum circuit. To evaluate the effectiveness of CLOAQ, we sample the input state uniformly from the Hilbert space of all qubits, which is more accurate than prior work that use all-|0〉 inputs. Our results show that CLOAQ benefits from the synergy between logic and phase protections. Compared with prior QCO approaches using only one perspective, the combined method is more resilient to attacks and causes greater functional disruption when the unlocking key is incorrect.

title: PhySeqForm: A Data-Driven, Physical Synthesis Sequence Former.
abstract: In the flow of digital IC design, physical synthesis optimizes a post-mapping design for subsequent physical design stages. During physical synthesis, netlist and layout information are modified to minimize leakage power while achieving timing closure. In practice, physical synthesis relies on discrete operators like buffer insertion and gate resizing, where the order of operators significantly impacts the optimization outcome. In this paper, we propose PhySeqForm, a data-driven, physical synthesis sequence spawner, which integrates a sampling-based estimation algorithm with a dynamic sequence generation strategy to customize efficient physical synthesis operator sequences. Our implementation outperforms the first-place results of MLCAD Contest 2025 by 6.3%.

title: A Unified Quantum Circuit Framework for Grover Search and Quantum Walks in NISQ Cryptanalysis.
abstract: This paper explores the use of quantum search in symmetric cryptanalysis within the Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) regime, introducing a unified quantum circuit framework that expresses Grover’s algorithm as a coined quantum walk. This enables a direct comparison of the two approaches, previously treated separately, under a common model of circuital resources and noise. The framework is implemented and tested on cyclic permutations and AES-like primitives. Experiments show that, in the ideal case, the walk exhibits the familiar Grover amplification curve although, under realistic depolarizing and readout noise, the peaks are damped and the optimal number of steps falls below the theoretical value. In the AES examples, the probability of recovering the key remains negligible. Taken together, these results extend earlier analyses and suggest that symmetric encryption maintains classical-level security in the NISQ era of quantum circuits, while also providing a reproducible testbed for future studies.

title: Additive Resource Scaling in Quantum Circuits for Search in Cryptanalysis.
abstract: Quantum search algorithms are often analyzed in idealized, isolated models, yet real hardware and cryptanalytic applications involve communication channels and residual entanglement. We develop a unified circuit framework that models these effects explicitly, introducing a controllable quantum-channel interaction between system and environment registers. The resulting non-isolated circuits exhibit additive time-space behavior, instead of standard multiplicative scaling. We provide circuit schematics, simulation data, and performance visualization demonstrating how a single-qubit environment modifies Grover oscillations and success probability trajectories of cryptographic attacks. The proposed framework connects algorithmic tradeoffs with measurable circuit phenomena, offering a practical methodology for quantum-classical hybrid circuits design.

title: An Asynchronous Mixed-Signal Resonate-and-Fire Neuron.
abstract: Analog computing at the edge is an emerging strategy to limit data storage and transmission requirements, as well as energy consumption, and its practical implementation is in its initial stages of development. Translating properties of biological neurons into hardware offers a pathway towards low-power, real-time edge processing. Specifically, resonator neurons offer selectivity to specific frequencies as a potential solution for temporal signal processing. Here, we show a fabricated Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) mixed-signal Resonate-and-Fire (R&F) neuron circuit implementation that emulates the behavior of these neural cells responsible for controlling oscillations within the central nervous system. We integrate the design with asynchronous handshake capabilities, perform comprehensive variability analyses, and characterize its frequency detection functionality. Our results demonstrate the feasibility of large-scale integration within neuromorphic systems, thereby advancing the exploitation of bio-inspired circuits for efficient edge temporal signal processing.

title: Probabilistic-Based Complementary Logic Gate Design.
abstract: When downscaling integrated circuits with a low supply voltage, noise can cause computing errors which decrease the reliability directly. Previous noise-tolerant designs trade too much reliability for area. In this paper, a probabilistic-based complementary logic gate design is proposed. It separates logic "1" and "0" signals into either robust bits and weak bits from the perspective of probability. The design tolerates errors from noise in terms of probability. By only choosing robust bits, the proposed logic gates can generate high quality output signals. Also, a general mapping rule is deduced to allow the idea to be easily implemented automatically within the existing Electronic Design Automation flows.

title: Data-driven Parameter Design Method for Memristive LIF Neuron Circuits.
abstract: Memristive leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron circuits have attracted considerable interest due to their compact size, structural simplicity, and low power consumption. However, existing parameter design methods for such circuits heavily rely on accurate mathematical models of the memristive device, which can be difficult to obtain. This paper presents an experimental data-driven approach for parameter design of memristive LIF neuron circuits. The proposed method begins by applying voltage and current sweeping to the memristors to characterize their static operating ranges and control types based on the Edge of chaos (EOC) definition. Subsequently, an AC small-signal excitation superimposed on a suitable DC bias is applied to analyze the frequency-domain response, enabling the determination of the type and parameters of additional circuit elements required for the neuron. To validate the method, a simple memristor model and its corresponding emulator circuit are implemented, confirming the correctness and feasibility of the proposed design strategy.

title: An RRAM-based Multi-Timescale Spiking Processor with Reconfigurable Neurons.
abstract: Real-world temporal data often exhibit multi-timescale dynamics. Liquid State Machine (LSM), as a type of Spiking Neural Networks, show remarkable ability in processing multi-timescale data with high performance and efficiency. However, LSMs inherently suffer from lack of flexibility caused by the fixed architecture. In this work, we demonstrate a novel LSM architecture for multi-timescale signal processing. This work captures both transient and long-term temporal characteristics in data with multiple timescales through a reconfigurable framework. The key innovation lies in both the algorithmic model with trainable neuron decay constants and physical implementation with resistive random-access-memory (RRAM) array. This work achieves significant benchmarks for edge deployment with RRAM array, delivering 97.6% 5-class ECG signal classification accuracy on the MIT- BIH database. It bridges the gap between algorithm and hardware, enabling effective and hardware-efficient multi-timescale data processing in real-world applications.

title: A Battery Management System Applied to Critical Remote Devices, Featuring High Transient Response and Battery-System Separate Charging.
abstract: This paper presents a battery management system (BMS) that extends battery lifespan for long-endurance applications such as satellites, remote IoT sensor nodes, and implantable medical devices. The proposed BMS employs a dual-mode control strategy: a four-switch buck-boost mode with fast load-current feedback for enhanced transient response, and a separated power-path mode employs dedicated paths for the system load and the battery that prevents battery charge-discharge cycling caused by system power fluctuations. The control IC is fabricated in a 0.18 μm BCD process. Simulation results demonstrate that the converter supports a wide input voltage range from 2.7 V to 18 V and an output range from 3 V to 18 V, utilizing a 2.2 μH inductor at a switching frequency of 600 kHz. With the load-current feedback mechanism, output voltage overshoot and current ripple are significantly reduced, achieving a V drop/I step ratio of 0.058 even at moderate switching frequencies. Moreover, the system delivers a maximum load current of 5 A with a peak efficiency of 96.74%.

title: Energy-Efficient Fall Detection Using Conditional Dual-Path Spiking Neural Networks with Hierarchical Temporal Dynamics.
abstract: Falls remain one of the leading causes of injury and mortality worldwide, underscoring the need for accurate and energy-efficient wearable detection systems. Existing deep neural networks achieve high recognition accuracy but require dense, always-on computation that is impractical for continuous monitoring. Meanwhile, current fall detection frameworks process all activities with the same high-resolution pipeline, wasting energy on steady daily motions that dominate most of the time. To address these challenges, we propose a conditional dual-path spiking framework based on Adaptive Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (ALIF) neurons. A steady-state path continuously monitors low-frequency daily activities at reduced sampling, while a transient-response path activates only when high-frequency motion or low-confidence predictions occur. This event-driven design dynamically allocates computation to salient motion periods, ensuring efficient and responsive operation. The proposed model achieves 98.6% overall accuracy on the KFall dataset, while reducing computation by 56.8% compared to dense ANN baselines.

title: Live Demonstration: A Dual-modal Neural Sensing Array System with Back-end Neural Signal Processing.
abstract: This live demonstration shows a dual-modal neural sensing array system with back-end neural signal processing. The implemented system includes a front-end 32×32 pixels LabOn-Chip array and a back-end python-based data sorting and processing engine to examine. Within the array, a dual mode recordings pixels is capable to capture both electrical recording channel and three chemical recording channels, with integrated sensors/electrodes, amplifiers and digitization circuits. The spacing between active pixels is only 100μm. The 1024 electrical recording channels and 3072 chemical recording channels can simultaneously collect electrical and chemical signals for in-vitro brain slice at the sampling rates of 10kHz and 3.3kHz. The back-end data processing engine collect the data, analysis the correlation between recording sites.

title: An Area-Efficient Neural Stimulator Chip Achieving 23V Voltage Compliance by 180nm BCD CMOS process.
abstract: Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) ameliorates pathological neural activity through the delivery of precisely regulated electrical impulses to targeted subcortical structures, thereby modulating aberrant neural circuit function and restoring normative physiological dynamics. One of the design challenges of DBS circuits is to fit the variable impedance of the electrode-tissue interface (ETI) by a high voltage compliance. Traditional neural stimulator ICs try to increase the voltage compliance by using either high-voltage (HV) process or a stacked configuration of standard MOSFETs, which lead to large chip areas or potential transistor breakdown. To address the issue, a current-steering shifter technique is proposed to offer the neural stimulator a high voltage compliance at the cost of a small chip area. The proposed technique is implemented into a neural stimulator chip fabricated in 0.18μm BCD CMOS technology. The measured results show that the proposed chip achieves 23V voltage compliance with 1.77mA maximum stimulation current, which takes a small chip area of only 0.2mm2per channel.

title: A ReMOS Cross-Coupled Charge Pump Achieving 0.62-V VDR and 81.5% Peak PCE for Micro Energy Harvesting Applications.
abstract: This paper presents a reconfigurable CMOS (ReMOS) cross-coupled charge pump (CCCP) that widens the input voltage (Vin) dynamic range (VDR) while maintaining high power conversion efficiency (PCE) for battery-assisted IoT/WSN applications. Fabricated in 130-nm CMOS technology, the proposed CCCP operates in 5 reconfigurable modes via a transistor reconfigurable method. Conduction efficiency (low ON-resistance) is enhanced in the low-power zone (LPZ) by increasing the effective width of the device dynamically, while leakage is effectively suppressed in the highpower zone (HPZ) by increasing the effective length of the device dynamically. Measured results show 81.5% peak PCE at 400-mV Vininto RL= 500 kΩ and a 623-mV VDR at PCE ≥ 30%. Compared with prior CMOS CCCPs, the proposed prototype demonstrates a wide efficient VDR and competitive peak efficiency.

title: Slack-Guided Arbitration for Network-on-Chip Congestion Mitigation in Boolean Processor Array Emulation.
abstract: Boolean Processor Array (BPA) architectures enable efficient emulation of large-scale integrated circuits by mapping circuit netlists onto hardware operators. However, irregular directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) create unpredictable data transfer patterns, causing network congestion that degrades emulation performance. Traditional FIFO arbitration fails to exploit task graph topology, resulting in suboptimal network utilization. We propose a slack-guided arbitration algorithm that dynamically schedules packet transmissions using task dependencies and critical path information computed via backward BFS with iterative refinement. Evaluations on 10 industrial benchmarks and synthetic workloads show average improvements of 6.46% for netlists and 24.82% for highly dense random graph, with up to 27.35% gains in contended scenarios.

title: EEschematic: Multimodal-LLM Based AI Agent for Schematic Generation of Analog Circuit.
abstract: Circuit schematics play a crucial role in analog integrated circuit design, serving as the primary medium for human understanding and verification of circuit functionality. While recent large language model (LLM)-based approaches have shown promise in circuit topology generation and device sizing, most rely solely on textual representations such as SPICE netlists, which lack visual interpretability for circuit designers. To address this limitation, we propose EEschematic, an AI agent for automatic analog schematic generation based on a Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM). EEschematic integrates textual, visual, and symbolic modalities to translate SPICE netlists into schematic diagrams represented in a human-editable format. The framework uses six analog substructure examples for few-shot placement and a Visual Chain-of-Thought (VCoT) strategy to iteratively refine placement and wiring, enhancing schematic clarity and symmetry. Experimental results on representative analog circuits, including a CMOS inverter, a five-transistor operational transconductance amplifier (5T-OTA), and a telescopic cascode amplifier, demonstrate that EEschematic produces schematics with high visual quality and structural correctness.

title: Hardware-Efficient Image Super-Resolution for Solid-State LiDARs Using Single-Pixel Imaging.
abstract: Macropixel architectures in SPAD-based solid-state LiDARs reduce data bandwidth but significantly degrade spatial resolution. This work proposes a single-pixel-imaging-inspired super-resolution method that sequentially enables individual SPADs within each macropixel and reconstructs per-SPAD histograms using inverse Hadamard transforms. Compared to the brute force approach that sequentially activates SPADs one by one, the proposed approach provides an SNR increase in the histogram by 2.84 for both subframes and the final super-resolved depth map. The proposed approach requires only minimal hardware modification and lightweight arithmetic operations. Experiments on a commercial LiDAR dataset show that the method restores fine spatial structure in both full- and partial-histogram modes without relying on machine learning or external accelerators.

title: A Monolithic 5×14-Channel Cryo-CMOS Multiplexer for Scalable Control of Trapped-Ion Qubits.
abstract: Trapped-ion quantum computing offers a promising path to scalability, which relies on high-fidelity voltage control across hundreds of dynamic electrodes. However, as systems grow in complexity, traditional room-temperature control architectures face severe wiring and signal transmission bottlenecks. This work presents a monolithic cryogenic CMOS multiplexer for scalable dynamic electrode control in trapped-ion quantum processors. Fabricated in the UMC 0.162 µm HV-CMOS process, the chip integrates 210 high-voltage analog switches, enabling 14-to-70 channel multiplexing with three conduction modes: forward, reverse, and compensation. A complementary transmission gate with a resistive negative feedback mechanism stabilizes the effective VGS, suppresses RONvariation, and enhances linearity at 4 K. Measurement results at 4 K demonstrate high signal fidelity (SNR > 61 dB), low crosstalk (4 MHz), and fast switching (< 1 µs), validating its suitability for cryogenic trapped-ion systems.

title: A Linear Analog Resonate-and-Fire Neuron.
abstract: Oscillatory dynamics have recently proven highly effective in machine learning (ML), particularly through State-Space-Models (SSM) that leverage structured linear recurrences for long-range temporal processing. Resonate-and-Fire neurons capture such oscillatory behavior in a spiking framework, offering strong expressivity with sparse event-based communication. While early analog RAF circuits employed nonlinear coupling and suffered from process sensitivity, modern ML practice favors linear recurrence. In this work, we introduce a resonate-and-fire (RAF) neuron, built in 22nm Fully-Depleted Silicon-on-Insulator technology, that aligns with SSM principles while retaining the efficiency of spike-based communication. We analyze its dynamics, linearity, and resilience to Process, Voltage, and Temperature variations, and evaluate its power, performance, and area trade-offs. We map the characteristics of our circuit into a system-level simulation where our RAF neuron is utilized in a keyword-spotting task, showing that its non-idealities do not hinder performance. Our results establish RAF neurons as robust, energy-efficient computational primitives for neuromorphic hardware.

title: Efficient Hardware-Oriented Approximation of Mish Activation Function and Its Realization.
abstract: The Mish activation function is widely utilized in fields such as computer vision, natural language processing, and remote sensing recognition. However, its complex nonlinear transcendental function results in significant computational overhead and poses challenges for hardware deployment. Existing piecewise linear or polynomial approximation methods struggle to balance neural network model performance with hardware efficiency, as higher accuracy typically entails greater computational costs. To address this issue, a hardware-friendly Mish approximation method based on piecewise polynomials is proposed. In the method, the optimal interval partitioning and the approximation function for each interval are determined simultaneously, by combining Particle Swarm Optimization and Symbolic Regression methods, with the objective of minimizing error subject to hardware constraints. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to previous Mish approximation methods, this method improves the accuracy of the approximated Mish function by up to 72.2%, leading to an improvement in the accuracy of typical neural network models by up to 1.4%; at the same time, hardware implementation of the proposed approximated Mish function reduces delay by 66.9%, area by 60.5% and power consumption by 80.5%.

title: Multi-stage Superpixel-guided Mamba-based Network for Change Detection.
abstract: Remote sensing image change detection relies on accurate modeling of multi-temporal features. Existing Mamba-based methods, however, often suffer from insufficient local information and redundant computations during feature aggregation, leading to inaccurate change boundary predictions. To address these issues, we introduce a superpixel mechanism into the Mamba-based framework and propose a Multi-stage Superpixel-guided Mamba Network for Change Detection (MSPMCD). In the encoder, a superpixel aggregation module extracts structurally consistent region-level features to enhance local and global representations, while a superpixel–pixel association matrix is constructed at the pre-event stage and updated at the post-event stage to preserve bi-temporal correlations. During feature fusion, superpixel-based regional constraints and feature proxy mechanisms enable region-level bi-temporal interaction. In addition, a superpixel consistency loss enforces similarity among pixel predictions within the same superpixel, ensuring intra-superpixel consistency and improving change boundary accuracy. Experiments on multiple public datasets demonstrate that MSPMCD achieves high F1 and IoU scores.

title: CML-UNet: An Adaptive Spatiotemporal Registration Network for Medical Image Sequences.
abstract: Deformable medical image registration underpins many diagnostic and therapeutic workflows. To address the complex spatiotemporal deformations induced by physiological motion in image sequences such as 4D CT, we propose CML-UNet, a registration network that jointly models large- scale spatial deformations and temporal dynamics. Built on UNet, the network introduces a new recurrent cell, CNN-Vision Mamba with Bidirectional LSTM (CM-BiLSTM), to leverage multi-frequency and time-domain features in concert. Compared with conventional CNN blocks, CM-BiLSTM unifies multi-scale parallel feature extraction and bidirectional long-range temporal modeling, enabling spatiotemporal information from both past and future frames to be jointly encoded at each stage. This design mitigates feature degradation during hierarchical propagation. In addition, we propose Adaptive Frequency Routing (AFR) that fuses high- and low-frequency features adaptively at multiple stages, guided by a frequency prior, thereby improving the overall representation. On two public 4D CT datasets, CML-UNet achieves TREs of 1.15 mm and 0.90 mm, surpassing prior methods and indicating potential for clinical application.

title: FPGA-Accelerated Fully Spectral CNNs for Real-Time Semantic Segmentation.
abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are vital for computer vision but suffer from high computational costs. Fully Spectral CNNs mitigate this using Fast Fourier Transforms (FFT) and frequency-domain activations; however, large inputs and spectral self-convolutions cause significant overhead in segmentation tasks. To address this, we propose the Overlapped Partitioning Block Method (OPBM), which divides large images into smaller overlapping blocks, reducing computation while maintaining spectral efficiency. We also design an FPGA-based accelerator with parallel, pipelined computing and performance modeling for further optimization. Experiments on CamVid and Cityscapes show that OPBM achieves a 1.4×~ 2.2× speedup over the full-input spectral baseline with only 0.1% ~ 0.9% accuracy loss, and up to 8.7× speedup over traditional spatial methods, demonstrating outstanding efficiency and scalability.

title: A Photovoltaic Energy-Harvesting Chip Featuring Self-Adaptive-Monitoring-Time MPPT.
abstract: The widespread deployment of Internet of Things (IoT) applications, such as wearable devices, environmental monitoring, smart homes, logistics tracking, and smart agriculture, has created a growing demand for lightweight devices with extended battery life. This necessitates the adoption of energy-harvesting technologies to resolve the inherent conflict between compact battery size and prolonged operational endurance. Among various energy-harvesting techniques, photovoltaic (PV) energy stands out due to its high energy density in various environment, offering a viable approach to prolong device runtime. However, as the ambient light intensity varies significantly versus environmental conditions, the maximum power point tracking (MPPT) becomes essential to improve the energy-harvesting efficiency. Conventional approaches employ the fractional open circuit voltage (FOCV) method in MPPT, which relies on a fixed predetermined monitoring time, leading to considerable energy loss versus the dynamic illumination variations. In this work, a novel FOCV technique based on self-adaptive monitoring time is proposed for MPPT, which reduces the energy loss of the PV energy-harvesting IC during the MPPT process, thereby effectively improving the overall energy conversion efficiency. Fabricated in 180nm CMOS process, the prototype chip demonstrates a 59.6% reduction in energy loss attributed to MPPT detection compared to conventional methods, achieving a measured peak efficiency of 88.2%.

title: An End-to-End Compilation Flow with Reinforcement Learning-Guided Logic Synthesis.
abstract: High-level synthesis (HLS) enables rapid accelerator generation from high-level descriptions but lacks coordination with downstream logic synthesis (LS), limiting optimization for area, performance, and latency. This paper presents CASCADE, a customizable compiler built on MLIR that integrates HLS and LS into a unified optimization framework. CASCADE bridges high-level models to hardware through domain-aware transformations across multiple abstraction levels, including memory layout specialization, operator fusion, and polyhedral analysis. To enhance hardware mapping efficiency, CASCADE introduces a reinforcement learning (RL) guided logic synthesis exploration module that works jointly with the HLS pipeline. This module adjusts synthesis parameters such as mapping strategy, logic restructuring, and technology-specific optimization under different design constraints. By embedding this adaptive exploration into the MLIR pass pipeline, CASCADE automatically tunes transformation sequences and synthesis directives to achieve balanced trade-offs among performance, area, and latency. Experiments show that CASCADE delivers consistent speedups and improved hardware efficiency compared with state-of-the-art system-level compilers across diverse accelerators and workloads.

title: A Digital Baseband ASIC Targeting 99.999% Fidelity for Qubit Control and Readout with ROI-based Classification.
abstract: As superconducting qubits scale toward large-scale quantum processors, conventional room-temperature (RT) control and readout architectures introduce interconnect bottlenecks that lead to high latency. To mitigate these issues, a cryogenic circuit architecture is adopted that co-integrates control and readout circuits with qubit chips within a cryo-environment. However, this approach is constrained by refrigerator limitations, which impose stringent requirements on area and power dissipation, while high-fidelity qubit operation necessitates high spectral purity. A 28 nm bulk-CMOS digital baseband ASIC is presented for qubit control and readout, integrating a pulse modulator capable of arbitrary-envelope modulation, a readout receiver with a state classifier for reflectometry-signal preprocessing, and on-chip state classification after offline training. Key techniques include (i) a multiplier-less CORDIC-based Direct Digital Synthesis (DDS) for high-precision pulse shaping, which replaces conventional LUT-based implementations and achieves a 29.2% higher speed and a 41.54% lower area compared to conventional LUT-based DDS, with SFDR > 54dB; (ii) a dynamic Region of Interest (ROI) based data cleansing method that classifies the qubit states from a small data subset, reducing memory requirements by 89% compared to conventional threshold classification approaches, while ensuring fidelity degradation is no more than 0.32% compared to the theoretical limit.

title: RASLL: A Removal Attack on SAT-Resistant Logic Locking.
abstract: Logic locking techniques have emerged as an active defense against intellectual property (IP) infringement in integrated circuit design, yet attacks targeting these techniques have coevolved. This paper proposes RASLL, a novel removal attack that extracts key-connected subcircuits by tracing the output paths of key-driven gates. It then constructs the subcircuit truth tables and derives pairs of key values and input patterns that produce true outputs, enabling recovery of the original circuit. Experimental evaluations based on ISCAS’85 and ISCAS’89 benchmark circuits show that, compared to Boolean satisfiability (SAT)-based attacks, the proposed RASLL recovers the complete set of key values and corresponding input patterns for all the benchmark circuits and reduces the computation time by more than 83%, while conventional removal attacks are inapplicable due to the absence of viable targets. To the best of our knowledge, RASLL represents the first successful attack on a variant of input-dependent key-based logic locking (IDKLL) techniques.

title: Energy-Efficient Neural Video Coding via a High-Throughput Hardware Design for Pointwise Convolution and LUT-based WSiLU.
abstract: Neural video codecs such as DCVC-RT achieve high compression efficiency but typically rely on high-end GPUs, leading to prohibitive power and energy in battery-powered devices. This paper presents an energy-efficient ASIC implementation of two core DCVC-RT primitives: the pointwise (1×1) convolution and the WSiLU activation. Additionally, we introduce a hardware-friendly LUT approximation for WSiLU that preserves coding efficiency, adding only 0.40% BD-Rate when integrated into DCVC-RT. Synthesized in 40 nm at 100 MHz, the design dissipates 238.82 mW and consumes 9.33 pJ per processed sample, yielding up to 731× lower energy than software execution on a high-end GPU of the same pointwise convolution + WSiLU operation. To the best of our knowledge, this is among the first dedicated hardware designs targeting learned video compression frameworks.

title: Design-Driven Exploration of MOM Capacitors for Capacitive Neural Networks.
abstract: Recent advances in capacitive network design have improved data converter performance; however, parasitic capacitances remain a key limitation to the computational accuracy and energy efficiency of capacitive neural networks. This work presents the design and analysis of a Metal-Oxide-Metal (MOM) based capacitive synapse, investigating parasitic effects across multiple existing interdigitated structures and proposing strategies for scalable, energy-efficient capacitor arrays. We demonstrate and quantify how structural variations and the aggregation of unit capacitors into larger structures introduce additional parasitic capacitances, degrading accuracy and energy efficiency. Under nominal conditions, the post-layout simulation results demonstrate excellent agreement between the analytical and simulated weighted-sum voltage node of a capacitive divider circuit in four structures and across two different methods. In contrast, a 4-bit input capacitive Artificial Neuron (AN) exhibits a deviation of 9–12% due to threshold logic and switch circuit parasitics, while energy consumption varies by approximately 1.2% between structures.

title: Modeling of an All-Mechanical In-Sensor Vibration Classifier Compatible with MEMS Implementation.
abstract: This work explores the feasibility of an electromechanical in-sensor intelligent timeseries classification system implemented using MEMS technology. The proposed architecture integrates, on a single chip, an acceleration sensing layer and a mechanical MEMS neuron for vibration features classification, eliminating the need for any digital interfacing or processing. The computing principles relies on the direct electromechanical coupling between the sensing mass and the MEMS neurons, so that capacitive transduction enables computation within the sensor itself. A neuron performs a mechanical summation of input forces followed by an electrostatically governed nonlinear activation, analogous to neural processing. Simulations of the system's constituent elements, on a toy example of classification task, demonstrate the compatibility of MEMS-based neuromorphic architectures with MEMS sensing units, paving the way for truly integrated mechanical intelligence at the edge.

title: Hardware-Aware Attractor Dynamics in Neuromorphic Systems: Compensating for Device Mismatch through Network Design.
abstract: Attractor networks and their underlying attractor dynamics represent a powerful computational primitive for implementing robust and reliable computations in neuromorphic systems. Their ability to sustain stable activity states makes them especially suitable for neuromorphic processing, where low-power, continuous-time operation is achieved by leveraging the intrinsic physics of analog circuits. However, device mismatch in analog circuits creates parameter variability that challenges traditional mean-field approaches relying on homogeneous population responses. We investigate how parameter variability affects recurrent excitatory-inhibitory networks, demonstrating that device mismatch creates heterogeneous response functions leading to distinct functional neuron classes. Our results show that systematic tuning of recurrent connectivity can compensate for hardware variability and maintain stable attractor states, with compensation strategies validated through successful implementation on mixed-signal analog/digital neuromorphic processors. We extend this framework to networks under periodic perturbations, revealing analogous functional segregation and identifying synaptic time constants as the key parameters distinguishing functional classes. Counterintuitively, networks with compensated variability prove more robust than homogeneous networks when subjected to input degradation. These findings provide practical design principles for implementing reliable attractor dynamics in analog neuromorphic hardware while leveraging parameter heterogeneity as a computational advantage.

title: Design of a PUF in 600-nm IGZO-TFT Flex-ICs for Secure IoT Applications.
abstract: This thesis presents an innovative Physically Unclonable Function (PUF) implemented in 600 nm Indium-Gallium-Zinc-Oxide (IGZO) Thin-Film Transistor (TFT) technology, fabri- cated on Flexible Integrated Circuits (FlexICs). The proposed architecture takes advantage of device level randomness to produce distinct and repeatable digital responses by utilizing the intrinsic Threshold Voltage (Vth) variability of IGZO TFTs as a physical entropy source. Oxide TFTs, as opposed to conventional Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS)-based implementations, enable compatibility with low temperature, large area and mechanically flexible substrates. This approach is particularly well suited for the next generation of Internet of Things (IoT) and wearable electronic systems. The circuit architecture is based on a differential current comparison mechanism, where two transistor arrays are sequentially evaluated and their discharge characteristics are compared to produce a digital output. Cadence Virtuoso transient simulations were statistically modeled using the experimentally extracted Vth distributions from manu- factured IGZO TFT matrices. This allowed for precise analysis of entropy quality and robustness. Nine National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) SP 800-22 statis- tical test suites were successfully passed by the resultant bitstreams, demonstrating high entropy and consistent randomness across several simulated instances. Additionally, transient noise simulations were performed to assess stability under process and environmental fluctuations. The bitstream demonstrated a Bit Error Ratio (BER) below 0.4% at the optimal comparator threshold. Overall, the proposed IGZO-TFT PUF demonstrates that thin-film oxide electronics can serve as a foundation for intrinsic, low cost and hardware-based security primitives, suitable for secure identification in flexible and large area electronic systems.

title: Enhancing Neuromorphic Pattern Selectivity for Imbalanced Data by Adapting from Homeostasis.
abstract: Neuromorphic systems are at the forefront of edgeconstrained learning applications due to their low-power and hardware-efficient mechanisms. Unsupervised neuromorphic algorithms use neurons to represent patterns within the data, commonly embedding homeostatic regulations to balance neuron firing rate and evenly distribute computational load among the available neurons. In real-world scenarios, datasets are often highly imbalanced and identification of rare features becomes critical. In such cases, homeostatic regulation encourages the algorithm to select for majority classes and become blind to the minority class. This work shows that the homeostatic assumption can be adapted within a simple Spiking Neural Network (SNN) classifier, to select for minority patterns under imbalanced, multiclass training conditions. A Base (homeostatic) and Adaptive model are first compared for a simple binary grayscale training set, demonstrating proof-of-concept. These models are then applied to the Modified National Institute of Standards and Technology (MNIST) handwritten digit dataset, under various conditions of imbalance, to demonstrate Adaptive selectivity of Class 4 and Class 9 with only 20% of their original training incidence. Challenges remain in demonstrating blanket performance improvement in terms of precision and recall as datasets become more balanced, emphasizing the criticality of initial model parameters.

title: A Hybrid FIR-IIR MASH DTDSM with Optimized Self-Coupling Filter for Robust Low-Amplitude Stability.
abstract: A novel hybrid FIR-IIR MASH DTDSM architecture with a self-coupling filter is proposed to address the trade-off between robustness and maximum stable amplitude in delta-sigma modulators. The central innovation stems from the simultaneous optimization of filter dynamics and bit-width allocation via convex programming, dynamically modifying the hybrid FIR-IIR transfer function under stability constraints derived from the Lee criterion. The self-coupling method merges finite and infinite impulse response elements, which results in accurate noise shaping and lower quantization noise power while preserving stability margins. The proposed method sets itself apart from traditional techniques by introducing dynamic bit-width scaling and phase compensation, which reduce harmonic distortion and group delay fluctuations. Simulation results show improved stability at low amplitudes and decreased NTF peaking, accomplished by simultaneous stability observation and coefficient adjustment. This work is particularly relevant to fields demanding precise analog-to-digital conversion with strict durability standards, including biomedical sensing and wireless communication systems.

title: Hardware-Efficient POSIT Based SVM Inference Engine for Intelligent Biomedical Systems.
abstract: Typically, in most portable health-checkup devices, the process of scanning & reporting runs concurrently, hence the demand for establishing intelligence on edge devices continues to rise. However, edge devices pose an acute shortage of resources and tighter power constraints towards achieving longer shelf life, yet faster and more real-time outcomes are desired. Hardware ML design is possibly the way forward, but a compute-intensive structure, with no compromise in accuracy levels, calls for a design innovation. Classical ML techniques, including Support Vector Machine (SVM) and others, fit better for these requirements over other dense neuron architectures of DNNs. This paper proposes an efficient, dataset-agnostic SVM inference engine using optimized Posit arithmetic for biomedical applications. Leveraging a linear SVM kernel, the design offers a lightweight alternative to neural networks and demonstrates improved efficiency and dynamic range over traditional floating-point, validated across multiple biomedical datasets from the Physionet database. Multiple Posit configurations, ranging from (8,2) to (16,4), are evaluated to explore trade-offs in precision, area, power, and performance. FPGA implementation results demonstrate 67.4% reduction in resource utilization at the cost of negligible accuracy drop. ASIC validation further confirms the benefits, showing a 25.2% reduction in silicon footprint, a 34.7% reduction in power consumption, and a slight overhead in computational delay with respect to the corresponding fixed and floating-point implementations. The work showcases a step towards determining an optimal Posit topology for the hardware engine to accelerate inference without compromising critical accuracy and diagnostic outcomes. All the design files are made freely available at [1] for further usage by the designers and research community.

title: ISAC for Intelligent Transportation: Ray-Tracing, Clutter Cancellation, and Sensing-Aided Beamforming.
abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) is rapidly gaining prominence as a foundational capability for intelligent transportation systems, allowing wireless networks to perform simultaneous data transmission and environmental sensing using shared resources. However, accurate performance evaluation of ISAC sys- tems remains challenging due to complex multipath propagation, high vehicular mobility, and rapidly time-varying channel conditions. This dissertation presents a unified simulation and algorithmic framework for ISAC in vehicular scenar- ios. A three-dimensional (3D) ray-tracing simulation platform is developed using the NVIDIA Sionna RT framework to model realistic wireless channels, includ- ing multipath effects, Doppler shifts, and environmental clutter. Based on this platform, an Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM)-based radar sensing algorithm incorporating Static Clutter Cancellation (SCC) is developed to enhance vehicle range and velocity estimation performance under strong ur- ban clutter conditions. Additionally, a sensing-based trajectory prediction algo- rithm is developed to support predictive beamforming through proactive beam alignment toward moving vehicles. Simulation results demonstrate measurable improvements in localization accuracy and communication reliability under high- mobility conditions compared to reactive, non-predictive beamforming schemes. The proposed framework provides a practical toolset for assessing and develop- ing advanced ISAC solutions tailored to next-generation intelligent transportation infrastructure.

title: Power Side-Channel Attacks in Nanosheet Circuits.
abstract: Pushing the boundaries of device scaling and advanced circuit design, the semiconductor industry is moving beyond FinFETs. The nanosheet field-effect transistor (NSFET) technology is among the most promising contenders, improving area efficiency and reducing power consumption. As NSFET technology progresses toward production, it becomes crucial to assess how vulnerable their power profiles are to leaking confidential information. Here, we evaluate the resilience of an advanced encryption standard (AES) circuit to power side-channel attacks (PSCAs). By using transistor-level NSFET device models and full-layout netlists with standard delay format (SDF) back-annotation, we capture realistic timing and switching activities, enabling accurate power simulations. We conduct correlation power analysis (CPA) with randomized sampling, enabling robust insights. We find that 1-sheet devices, lower supply voltages, and stronger aging consistently provide superior resilience.

title: An Automated Framework for Optimal Selection of Approximate Computing Units for Low-Complexity Trigonometric Transforms on FPGAs.
abstract: The optimal selection of approximate computing units towards low-complexity FPGA-based hardware architectures for approximate discrete cosine transform (ADCT) and approximate discrete Fourier transform (ADFT) are explored. The proposed methodology employs an existing library of FPGA based approximate adders to select Pareto-optimal1approximate adders for cascaded signal flow architectures found in ADCT and ADFT operations. Benefits are presented with examples from 8-point ADCT based image compression and 16-point ADFT based digital multi-beamforming applications. Examples demonstrate a nearly 25% LUT reduction in FPGA utilization compared to error-free computing, with a corresponding degradation of nearly 1 dB in terms of PSNR in image compression and 0.3 dB loss in SNR improvement in beamforming.

title: Low-Complexity Multi-beamforming with Configurable Beam Profiles via Approximate-DSFT.
abstract: Low-complexity digital multi-beamforming via multiplier-less approximations for discrete spatial Fourier transform (DSFT) is explored. The proposed approach employs an approximate-DSFT (ADSFT) which - for a uniform linear array with N antennas producing N simultaneous beams, reduces the hardware multiplier requirement from 3N2to 0 with marginal error in the beam profiles. Importantly, the proposed approach extends the previously reported approximate discrete Fourier transform (ADFT) multi-beamforming systems having fixed beam profiles to enable configurable beam profiles, where the user can obtain N simultaneous beams within a given spatial angular region. Simulations demonstrate that the multi-beam profiles are largely accurate, and approximate selection results in deviations for 8- and 16-element ULAs, with worst-case beam angle errors of 0.3° and 0.2°, and worst-case sidelobe deviations of 1.7 dB and 1.4 dB, respectively. For the same scenarios, the proposed ADSFT provides 100% reduction in multiplier complexity and 44.45% reduction in adder complexity compared to conventional multi-beamforming algorithms.

title: A 94.3%-Efficient Battery-Less Wireless Sensor Node Featuring -0.5°C~+1°C Inaccuracy Room Temperature Two-Point Calibrated Sensor.
abstract: This paper presents a battery-less wireless sensor node that integrates energy harvesting with a room-temperature two-point calibratable temperature sensor. By utilizing ambient energy, the system eliminates the need for batteries and enables long-term, maintenance-free operation suitable for large-scale IoT deployments. The proposed temperature sensor performs offset and slope calibration entirely at room temperature using a digitally switchable resistor network, eliminating the need for costly multi-temperature testing. This approach simplifies production and improves yield without compromising accuracy. The system achieves -0.5°C~+1°C sensing inaccuracy after digital calibration and incorporates a power converter with 94.3% peak efficiency over a wide input range. Fabricated using a 130nm BCD process for the energy harvesting part and a 55nm ULP RF process for the BLE transceiver part, the platform combines energy efficiency with robust wireless performance.

title: Memristive probabilistic neuron enhanced memristor-based Ising machine for efficient combinatorial optimization.
abstract: Combinatorial Optimization Problems (COPs) are prevalent across many fields and are mostly NP-hard, posing significant challenges for conventional von Neumann architectures. Ising machines offer a promising alternative by mapping COPs onto spin systems that evolve toward low-energy states. Recent efforts have implemented Ising machines using various technologies, yet silicon-based approaches often suffer from limited parallelism and high energy consumption due to data movement and complex digital sampling. In this paper, we propose a memristor-based Ising machine scheme enhanced by probabilistic neurons that enable analog in-memory annealing. By performing spin updates directly in the analog domain, our architecture eliminates the need for high-precision ADCs and integrates intrinsic stochasticity for efficient exploration of the solution space without extra cost. Our proposed scheme can be easily integrated into existing memristor-based Ising machines and achieves approximately 100% improvement in energy efficiency.

title: Algorithm-Aided Design and Verification for Multiple-Node-Upset-Recovery Latches.
abstract: In advanced CMOS technologies, integrated circuits are becoming increasingly sensitive to soft errors in radiation environments. The design process of existing latches heavily relies on electronic design automation (EDA) tools with comprehensive error-injection-based robustness verification. In this paper, algorithm-aided design and verification for robust latches are proposed and then, three algorithm-aided latches (i.e., SURLAD, DURLAD, and TURLAD) respectively providing SNU-, DNU-, and TNU-recovery are proposed. These latches are recoverable from single-node-upsets (SNUs) and multiple-node upsets (MNUs), respectively. Verification results demonstrate the robustness and advantages in terms of delay and power overhead of the proposed latches compared with state-of-the-art latches.

title: A Neural Spike Sorting Framework with Multi-Scale Slope Detection and Lite-CNN Classification.
abstract: In invasive brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), achieving accurate and efficient spike sorting is hindered by the noise sensitivity of conventional methods and the high computational overhead of deep learning approaches. This paper proposes a hardware-efficient end-to-end solution combining Multi-Scale Slope-based Spike Detection (MS-SSD) and a Lightweight CNN (Lite-CNN). MS-SSD achieves a 99.91% recall rate through band-pass filtering, slope analysis, and multi-scale thresholding, while the Lite-CNN performs fine-grained classification and noise rejection on an optimized 5-sample temporal region-of-interest (ROI). Experimental results on the public Quiroga dataset demonstrate a classification accuracy of 99.08%. Remarkably, the proposed architecture requires only 34 Multiply-Accumulate operations (MACs) and 35 parameters per classification, making it highly suitable for resource-constrained, real-time BCI applications in edge computing scenarios.

title: Experimental Evaluation of a Varactor-Tuned Programmable Metasurface with Modular Electronics - Toward ASIC Integration.
abstract: Programmable metasurfaces are poised to reshape wireless communication and sensing, yet their adoption depends critically on the electronics that bias hundreds to thousands of reconfigurable elements. This paper reports measured results from a modular, 4.15 GHz programmable metasurface controlled by off-the-shelf electronics. The 256-element array achieves ~15 dB gain and ~100° beam steering, with 230 ms reconfiguration latency and 2.55 W power consumption per tile. However, some applications demand sub-100 ms and strict energy budgets. To satisfy such requirements, the manufactured prototype measurements are compared with post-layout simulations of a custom application-specific integrated circuit approach. The possibility of replacing the digital-to-analog converters with custom designed integrated circuits is explored to reduce per-tile power consumption, enabling battery or solar-powered operation and denser tiling. Latency still remains constrained if the same microcontroller-based control is used, but if a parallel control of the chips is adopted, it can reach the sub-millisecond updates required for mobile use cases. The comparison demonstrates how chip-based metasurfaces can reduce energy consumption and latency.

title: A Rate-Distortion-Complexity Analysis of Neural Video CODECs.
abstract: We study the decision-making process for choosing video compression systems through a rate-distortion- complexity (RDC) analysis. We use a Lagrangian cost D + λR + γC, such that choosing the best video codec among a number of candidates for an application demands selecting appropriate (λ, γ) values. Thus, we argue that an application may be associated with a (λ, γ) point, so that all possibilities of (λ, γ) span all the application space. An example streaming application was given as a case study. Furthermore, we can span the plane and compare codecs for the entire application space filled with different (λ, γ) choices. We then compared several state-of-the-art neural video codecs using the proposed metrics. Results are informative and surprising. We found that, within our RDC computation constraints, only a few neural video codecs came out as the best suited for any application, depending on where its desirable (λ, γ) lies.

title: Radiation-Hardened Circuit for Chaos-Based Characterization of Cosmic Ray Dynamics in Space Missions.
abstract: This paper presents a radiation-hardened circuit for characterizing cosmic ray dynamics using chaos theory. The proposed system identifies chaotic behavior in real time by reconstructing the Takens attractor and computing Lyapunov exponents. Experimental data include ground-based neutron flux measurements and charged particle data from the Galileo mission to Jupiter. The results indicate that cosmic ray interactions can be modeled as a deterministic chaotic system. When interacting with semiconductor devices, cosmic rays may induce single-event upsets (SEUs), observed as bit-flips in SRAM cells. The proposed circuit estimates the time intervals between SEUs, enabling a predictive fault-tolerance approach for spaceborne electronics and in situ monitoring of cosmic radiation.

title: Live Demonstration: Transformer-Based Visual Object Detection and Tracking on MPSoC.
abstract: Visual object detectors with transformers are very demanding models for hardware constrained devices such as FPGAs or custom solutions. This live demonstration shows a design that integrates our own nano version of the off-the-shelf RT-DETR transformer with a custom tracker. The tracker keeps the identity of a given face for its whole trajectory while in the field of view of the camera, addressing the lack of detections at faster frame rates.

title: SCONE: A Practical, Constraint-Aware Plug-in for Latent Encoding in Learned DNA Storage.
abstract: DNA storage has matured from concept to practical stage, yet its integration with neural compression pipelines remains inefficient. Early DNA encoders applied redundancy-heavy constraint layers atop raw binary data-workable but primitive. Recent neural codecs compress data into learned latent representations with rich statistical structure, yet still convert these latents to DNA via naive binary-to-quaternary transcoding, discarding the entropy model's optimization. This mismatch undermines compression efficiency and complicates the encoding stack. A plug-in module that collapses latent compression and DNA encoding into a single step. SCONE performs quaternary arithmetic coding directly on the latent space in DNA bases. Its Constraint-Aware Adaptive Coding module dynamically steers the entropy encoder's learned probability distribution to enforce biochemical constraints-GC balance and homopolymer suppression-deterministically during encoding, eliminating post-hoc correction. The design preserves full reversibility and exploits the hyperprior model's learned priors without modification. Experiments show SCONE achieves near-perfect constraint satisfaction with negligible computational overhead (< 2% latency), establishing a latent-agnostic interface for end-to-end DNA-compatible learned codecs.

title: Toward Generative Silicon: The Next Frontier in Open-Source and AI-Driven Analog Design.
abstract: Integrated circuit (IC) design is undergoing a noticeable shift as AI-assisted tools and code-driven layout frameworks begin to influence established workflows. Automation has reshaped digital design over the past two decades. However, analog and mixed-signal design remains largely manual and dependent on layout expertise, device intuition, and iterative refinement. In practice, analog design has become the point at which current methodologies struggle most and, therefore, the area in which new approaches are emerging first. Recent work on programmatic layout, such as gLayout, shows that expressing circuits as structured code rather than fixed geometry allows new forms of interaction, including automatic generation, refinement, and correction based on feedback. In parallel, large language models are beginning to work with design intent and constraints, not just code templates, suggesting a shift in how tools may participate in the process. This paper describes the current stage of this transition. It discusses the main technical obstacles—verification, evaluation, data availability, and trust—and argues that machine-interpretable circuit representations may be a necessary step toward more scalable design automation.

title: Jitter Reduction in Voltage Controlled Oscillators for Clocking at Cryogenic Temperature.
abstract: Operating Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor (CMOS) at cryogenic temperature offers multitude of advantages including higher device ON current, lower subthreshold leakage, superior switching characteristics, lower thermal noise floor, better digital noise margins etc. Generating high fidelity clocks at low temperature thus becomes critical for achieving high performance. The devices, however, demonstrate higher flicker noise at low temperature giving rise to higher phase noise in clock generation circuit components like voltage-controlled oscillators which further translate to higher jitter. We propose a new method of reverse body biasing to reduce the phase noise and jitter at cryogenic temperature when conventional techniques like supply voltage reduction do not yield expected returns. In this simulation study, we fit BSIM models to measured device I-V and noise data on 22nm Fully Depleted Silicon on Insulator (FDSOI) and show the improvement in the jitter and phase noise performance with our new proposed method.

title: A Time-Domain Verification Framework for Digitally-Trained Op Amp and Ring-Oscillator Based Analog Spiking Neural Network.
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) implemented using analog circuits offer substantial energy efficiency compared to digital realizations, but verifying their time-domain behavior remains challenging. Analog neurons, such as op-amp and ringoscillator (RO)-based leaky integrate-and-fire models, exhibit nonlinear dynamics that can diverge from their digitally trained counterparts, particularly at high spike rates due to discretization approximations like the bilinear transform. To address these challenges, we present a time-domain verification and visualization framework that allows users to configure network architectures, neuron models, including a new RO-based neuron architecture, and spike encoding schemes, and automatically generates Simulink-based simulations that reproduce analog dynamics. The framework provides real-time visualization of spiking activity, membrane potentials, and layer-wise dynamics, enabling both educational exploration and practical debugging. Demonstrations on the Iris dataset show that the framework achieves waveform-equivalent behavior to transistor-level simulations in Cadence Spectre while providing over an order-of-magnitude speedup. By combining interactive visualization with configurable neuron models, including the novel RO neuron, the framework offers an intuitive platform for understanding and verifying analog SNNs.

title: A Miniaturized In-Mouth pH Sensing System for Real-Time lntraoral Telemetry.
abstract: Dental caries is one of the most common chronic diseases worldwide, caused by acid production from bacterial metabolism of fermentable carbohydrates and affecting people of all ages. To evaluate the cariogenic and erosive properties of widely consumed food products, such as energy drinks, intraoral pH changes are measured during consumption. The gold standard for such measurements is miniaturized silicon-lithium-barium glass membrane electrodes. These electrodes allow dental plaque to form on their surface, thereby enabling in situ monitoring of pH changes in a biologically relevant environment. Due to their high impedance and susceptibility to external interference, they can currently only be measured using a large analog amplification and recording unit, which is highly limiting for study design and participant comfort, as individual measurements can take upwards of an hour. This work presents the first battery-powered, low-power wireless and wearable pH telemetry evaluation system designed for real-time intraoral pH monitoring with glass electrodes. The system comprises a miniaturized pH telemetry front-end, a neck-worn Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) node, and software tools for data acquisition, visualization, and reporting. The front end integrates with a custom dental prosthesis, directly digitizing the pH signal in the mouth and minimizing noise. The data is transmitted over BLE to a host computer, and analyzed using dedicated software that supports calibration, drift compensation, region marking, and PDF report generation. The system integrates an 8.6 by 3.3mm, 0.2g pH front-end and a 37.6g neck-worn BLE node which consume 8.89 mW to transmit data at 10 Hz to a host computer during a measurement. A five-hour continuous validation using standard calibration solutions (pH 4, 7, 10) demonstrates system stability with a drift of only 0.005 pH/min, and an effective response rate of 1.875 pH/s, confirming robust sensing and reliable wireless telemetry.

title: Compressive Light-Field Image Coding with Spatial-Angular Measurement Prediction.
abstract: Light Field (LF) images capture scene information across both spatial and angular dimensions, enabling rich 3D visual effects but producing massive data volumes. Conventional pixel-based and learning-based codecs achieve high compression efficiency but require heavy computation for reconstruction and rate-distortion (R-D) optimization at the encoder, making them impractical for resource-constrained capture environments. To address this issue, we propose an asymmetric LF compression framework operating in the measurement domain. In the proposed method, each view is reordered according to the proposed serpentine scan and projected into a low-dimensional measurement space via block compressive sensing (BCS). This process allows both spatial and angular correlations to be efficiently compressed through measurement-domain prediction without requiring pixel reconstruction. Additionally, mode decision and coding are performed directly on the measurements, eliminating iterative R-D optimization and, together with the dimensionality reduction effect of CS, significantly reducing encoder complexity. The proposed encoder demonstrated a significant speed advantage on standard LF benchmarks, achieving up to 5 times faster encoding than HEVC and over 10 times faster than VVC at a comparable visual quality of around 35.8 dB. Furthermore, the proposed serpentine scan order preserves angular adjacency, enabling stable spatial-angular prediction and improved R-D performance.

title: An Ultra-Low-Power Energy-Harvesting Wireless Transmitter with Nanowatt Duty-Cycled Operation for Autonomous Sensor Networks.
abstract: This paper presents and investigates an ultra-low-power wireless transmitter (TX), fabricated in a standard 130nm BiCMOS technology for energy-harvesting sensor network applications, and demonstrates its operation when powered by a thermoelectric generator (TEG). The proposed ultra-low-power transmitter enables battery-less short-range communication while maintaining a compact feature size. To achieve low-power operation, the transmitter employs injection-locking and frequency-multiplication techniques for ultra-low-power frequency synthesis, combined with on–off keying (OOK) modulation and an integrated duty-cycling mechanism for further power reduction. Operating in the 433MHz ISM band and supplied by dual voltages of 0.25V and 0.9V, the TX delivers –21dBm output power with a continuous-mode power consumption of approximately 100µW. Under aggressive duty-cycling, the average power is reduced to the nanowatt range (≈ 150nW), enabling operation from a compact thermoelectric generator driven by a small body-to-ambient temperature difference (ΔT2. These results demonstrate a significant advancement toward fully integrated, energy-autonomous wireless transmitters for wearable and industrial Internet-of-Things (IoT) applications.

title: Resistive switching of 2D material incorporated polymer based self-healing flexible memristor.
abstract: The composition of materials have a profound influence on the distinct resistance-switching characteristics of memristors. This study involves the fabrication and characterization of a self healing memristor device with copper electrodes on a glass substrate, having Poly Vinyl Alcohol (PVA)-reduced graphene oxide (PVA-rGO) or PVA-graphene switching layers in the configurations of Cu/PVA-rGO/Cu and Cu/PVA-graphene/Cu. XRD, SEM, and FTIR analyses provided insights into the composition and morphology of the switching layers, establishing a connection between device functionality and material properties. The resistive switching and memory characteristics of the device have been explored by means of Current-voltage (I-V) measurements, log I-V curve analysis, and potentiation/depression investigations. The PVA-rGO system exhibits a lower SET voltage compared to the PVA-graphene memristor. Furthermore, LTSPICE simulations were employed to analyze switching characteristics, aiming to replicate electrical responses and verify with the experimental I-V data. The results indicate the promise of PVA-based switching layers in memristor fabrication and proposed methods to enhance device performance for practical applications.

title: GUARDIAN: A Decoupled GNN Framework for Type-aware Hardware Trojan Detection.
abstract: With increased outsourcing of intellectual property (IP) cores to third-party vendors, system-on-chip designs face heightened security risks from hardware trojans (HTs) that can compromise integrity and functionality. Prior HT detection works typically train separate deep-learning models on combinational (TRTC-TC) and sequential (TRTC-TS) trojan benchmarks from the LEDA-based Trust-Hub dataset, treating them independently and framing detection as binary classification, which fails when both trojan types coexist in a single netlist. In contrast, our proposed method employs a unified Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based model trained on a mixed dataset comprising benchmarks from both TRTC-TC and TRTC-TS, enabling multi-class classification to distinguish between benign, combinational, and sequential trojans. The approach addresses key GNN constraints and attains strong detection performance on the mixed dataset: TPR of 99.3% and 100%, TNR of 99.99% and 99.9%, and PPV of 97.9% and 97% for combinational and sequential trojans, respectively.

title: SRAM-Based Compute-in-Memory Accelerator for Linear-decay Spiking Neural Networks.
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) have emerged as a biologically inspired alternative to conventional deep networks, offering event-driven and energy-efficient computation. However, their throughput remains constrained by the serial update of neuron membrane states. While many hardware accelerators and Compute-in-Memory (CIM) architectures efficiently parallelize the synaptic operation (W × I) achieving $\mathcal{O}(1)$ complexity for matrix–vector multiplication, the subsequent state update step still requires $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time to refresh all neuron membrane potentials. This mismatch makes state update the dominant latency and energy bottleneck in SNN inference. To address this challenge, we propose an SRAM-based CIM for SNN with Linear Decay Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LD-LIF) Neuron that co-optimizes algorithm and hardware. At the algorithmic level, we replace the conventional exponential membrane decay with a linear decay approximation, converting costly multiplications into simple additions while accuracy drops only around 1%. At the architectural level, we introduce an in-memory parallel update scheme that performs in-place decay directly within the SRAM array, eliminating the need for global sequential updates. Evaluated on benchmark SNN workloads, the proposed method achieves a 1.1× to 16.7× reduction of SOP energy consumption, while providing 15.9× to 69× more energy efficiency, with negligible accuracy loss relative to original decay models. This work highlights that beyond accelerating the W×I computation, optimizing state-update dynamics within CIM architectures is essential for scalable, low-power, and real-time neuromorphic processing.

title: A Temperature-Adaptive Bias Generator with Threshold-Voltage Compensation from 3.6 K to 410 K.
abstract: In this paper, we present a temperature-adaptive bias generator (TABG) with threshold-voltage compensation, which is capable of operating from high to deep cryogenic temperatures. The threshold voltage of metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs) increases by several hundred millivolts from high to deep cryogenic temperatures, which shifts the circuit’s operating point and may even lead to functional failure. To address this challenge, we propose a compact, low-power threshold-voltage compensated temperature-adaptive bias generator. The proposed design comprises two stacked MOSFETs with specifically selected aspect ratios. One diode-connected MOSFET with an inverse aspect ratio serves as a microampere-level, low-temperature-dependence current source. The other MOSFET, of the same type but with a large aspect ratio, converts a constant bias into a temperature-adaptive bias voltage, whose temperature sensitivity is approximately equal to that of the threshold voltage. Fabricated using a 0.18 μm process, the proposed design occupies an area of 328 μm2, consumes 28 µW, and has been validated to operate in an ultra-wide temperature range from 3.6 K to 410 K.

title: Analysis and Evolution of Dynamics in 1R Memristive Crossbars: From Sneak Currents to Analog Computing.
abstract: Memristors have shown strong potential for constructing compact and efficient computing systems. The 1R memristor crossbar offers a regular structure capable of representing multi-level memory states through analog resistance variations. While sneak currents in nanoscale memristor crossbars are often considered a challenge for reliable memory operation, this work demonstrates that they can instead be harnessed to build nonlinear dynamical systems for computation. We first explore and analyze the behavior of sneak currents in 1R memristor crossbars under different input–ground configurations, showing how these currents can be exploited to form useful dynamic responses. We then propose an evolutionary algorithm that automatically determines the assignment of input and ground signals, optimizing both their positions and timing. This strategy allows circuit synthesis without auxiliary components, relying solely on the memristor crossbar. Finally, the evolved crossbar configurations are applied to multi-task time-series prediction, showing improved accuracy and efficiency over conventional approaches. The findings confirm the promise of 1R memristor crossbars as a compact and effective platform for nonlinear dynamical computation.
