title: A Passive Threshold-Voltage-Mismatch Cancellation Technique for Visual-Neuron-Inspired HDR CMOS Image Sensors.
abstract: This paper addresses the critical issue of high fixed-pattern noise (FPN) caused by source-follower threshold-voltage (Vth) mismatch in high-dynamic-range (HDR) CMOS image sensor (CIS) inspired by visual neuronal response. We propose a threshold-voltage-mismatch cancellation technique that employs a simple capacitor-based sampling network to dynamically store and cancel pixel-specific Vthoffsets during the quantization phase. This approach effectively suppresses FPN without requiring power-intensive operational amplifiers or complex digital circuitry. Pre-layout simulation results in a 180 nm CMOS process demonstrate that under significant process induced Vthvariations, the proposed technique reduces the standard deviation of output digital codes from 11.56 LSB to 1.04 LSB, achieving 91.0% suppression of Vth-induced FPN. The circuit architecture introduces zero static power overhead, making it ideally suited for high-quality bio-inspired vision sensing in ultra-low-power Internet of Things applications.

title: A 65nm 8GHz E-PPWM/FSK IR-UWB Transceiver Achieving 2.4Gb/s Data Rate and 8.6pJ/b Energy Efficiency.
abstract: This paper presents a high-data-rate impulse-radio ultra-wideband (IR-UWB) transceiver for brain-computer interface (BCI) systems. To address the challenges of Gb/s data transmission under strict power constraints, a hybrid modulation scheme combining differential-coded extended pulse position/width modulation (E-PPWM) and frequency shift keying (FSK) is proposed. The transmitter employs a direct up-conversion architecture with a digital-controlled oscillator (DCO), while the receiver features a dual-path regenerative demodulator that reuses key circuit blocks for both envelope and frequency detection. Implemented in 65nm CMOS, the transceiver achieves a data rate of 2.4Gb/s with a power consumption of 20.6mW, demonstrating an energy-efficient solution for high-throughput neural data transmission.

title: A Layer-Aware Heterogeneous SNN Accelerator Architecture for Energy-Efficient Inference on Resource-Limited FPGAs.
abstract: Deploying fully connected Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) on resource-constrained FPGAs is challenging due to irregular memory access, high control complexity, and inefficient resource utilization caused by uniform neuron processing across all layers. To address these issues, we introduce a layer-aware heterogeneous accelerator architecture guided by empirical analysis of temporal spike sparsity. Our investigation reveals that early layers exhibit stable and sparse spike patterns, while deeper layers show dynamic variability. Leveraging this insight, the first hidden layer adopts a preloaded, time-multiplexed structure to eliminate redundant memory access, whereas deeper layers retain event-driven computation to accommodate dynamic activity. A fine-grained inter-layer pipelined scheduler further enables cycle-level parallelism across layers with minimal control overhead. Implemented on a low-cost Artix-7 FPGA (Basys3) using 4-bit quantization, the proposed design achieves 98.3% accuracy on MNIST, 78.5 kFPS throughput, and 6.07 μJ/sample energy consumption—offering over 140× improvement in energy efficiency over prior SNN accelerators on the same platform. This work provides a scalable and hardware-efficient solution for real-time SNN inference at the edge.

title: A 454.9-kHz, 65,100-NAND2-Equivalent-Gate Flexible Cortex-M0 SoC in 3-μm LTPS TFT Technology.
abstract: Flexible electronics have attracted increasing attention for emerging applications such as wearable healthcare and bio-integrated systems. Despite recent progress in flexible microprocessors, challenges remain in achieving high operating frequency, large-scale integration, and system scalability for flexible circuits. To address these limitations, we present the design of a flexible system-on-chip (SoC) based on a 3-μm low-temperature polycrystalline silicon (LTPS) complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) thin-film transistor (TFT) technology. A comprehensive digital design methodology tailored for the LTPS process is established, including device characterization, digital standard cell library design and development, register-transfer level (RTL) design, logic synthesis, and physical implementation, with process-specific optimizations to enhance the speed, power efficiency, and reliability. Leveraging this framework, we have implemented a 32-bit programmable Cortex-M0-based SoC, integrating on-chip memory, AHB/APB bus interconnects, and multiple peripheral modules. Post-layout simulations validate that the SoC achieves a maximum operating frequency of 454.9 kHz and integrates approximately 65,100 NAND2-equivalent gates. To our knowledge, these metrics represent new benchmark for performance and integration scale for flexible circuits. This work demonstrates the feasibility of large-scale, high-performance flexible SoC design using LTPS TFT technology and provides a design paradigm to accelerate the development of sophisticated flexible systems.

title: Slice-Aware Sampling in CS-based Deep Learning Brain MRI Reconstruction.
abstract: Deep Neural-based reconstruction for Compressed Sensing (CS) has emerged as a powerful approach for accelerating brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), minimizing scan duration and patient discomfort, surpassing traditional methods. Among the numerous available architectures, ADMM-CSNet stands out as one of the most effective state-of-the-art solutions. However, this approach is affected by a high standard deviation in the reconstruction accuracy. In this work, we investigate the cause of this variability. Specifically, we show that brain MRI itself has a high variability in information content, meaning that the first and last sections are relatively simple to reconstruct, while central views are more complex.To overcome this problem, we adopt the Weighted Random Sampling (WRS) strategy, enhancing both reconstruction quality and robustness. Although this is not typically applied to this kind of dataset, it allows a refinement of the ADMM-CSNet framework, directing the network’s learning process to prioritize central slices over lateral slices. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach consistently outperforms the baseline ADMM-CSNet and other state-of-the-art methods in terms of mean achieving a 22% lower standard deviation than the original model. Finally, the experimental results on pathological MRI images further validate the efficacy of the proposed method, showing an average PSNR gain of 3 dB over the original baseline.

title: Graph-Structure-Aware Hyperdimensional Computing for Hardware Trojan Detection.
abstract: State-of-the-art hardware Trojan (HT) detection largely relies on machine learning (ML)–especially GNNs– whose multi-layer message passing with learnable weights incurs substantial computation. This paper proposes a graph-structure-aware hyperdimensional computing (HDC) framework for netlist-level HT detection: we modify an open-source pipeline’s feature engineering to produce HDC-compatible graph features and inject k-hop directed structure via HDC binding and bundling, markedly improving sensitivity to HT nodes. Using HDC encoding and similarity inference, the method achieves TNR 99.82%, TPR 96.99%, and F1 89.56% on Trust-HUB, comparable to mainstream GNNs, while requiring only one-shot projection and prototype aggregation, no learnable weights, and bit-level operations–yielding low training/inference cost, easy parallelism, and suitability for resource-constrained edge deployments.

title: Reinforcement Learning Framework with Improved NSGA-II for Logic Synthesis.
abstract: Exponentially expanding design space in logic synthesis poses significant challenges for AI-driven high-performance computing (AI-HPC) in logic optimization. Reinforcement learning (RL), as a key of AI-HPC, performs well in searching for solutions but converges poorly, whereas heuristic algorithms converge excellently yet begin from low-quality solutions. This paper proposes a hybrid high-performance AI computing framework for FPGA logic optimization that combines RL with an improved Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II). This framework integrates the strengths of both RL and NSGA-II. Specifically, an Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C) agent is employed as an initial population generator to produce a high-quality and diverse set of solutions. The improved NSGA-II, incorporating structure-aware hashing to avoid redundant evaluations, along with adaptive crossover and mutation mechanisms, is then applied to efficiently optimize multiple objectives. Compared with resyn2, evaluation results on the EPFL benchmark suite and FPGA mapping demonstrate that the proposed framework reduces the LUT-6 count by an average of 14.82% under delay constraints.

title: Topology-Aware GNN Embedding with Domain Priors and Graph Policy Regularization for Balanced Multi-Objective Analog IC Design.
abstract: Analog integrated circuit (IC) sizing is challenging due to its high-dimensional parameter space, stringent design constraints, and the need to balance conflicting objectives like gain, bandwidth, power, and stability. Conventional GCN-RL frameworks often use graph neural networks (GNNs) as passive feature extractors, leading to weak coupling between topology representation and policy learning. This paper proposes a Graph-Regularized Twin-Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient framework that integrates graph-based circuit embeddings with reinforcement learning. Circuit topologies are encoded through flexible GNNs, enriched with domain-specific priors such as pole-zero distribution, gain-bandwidth product, and phase margin. The embeddings are processed by a Graph Policy Regularization (GPRO) module to enforce structural consistency and improve TD3 policy. An adaptive exploration strategy enhances sampling efficiency. SPICE-in-the-loop experiments show that GPRO-TD3 achieves faster convergence, more stable trade-offs, and superior generalization compared to vanilla TD3 and evolutionary baselines.

title: An Optimized Pre-Emphasis Spike Detector for High-Density Neural Interfaces.
abstract: Spike detection plays a core role in neural signal processing and brain-computer interfaces (BCIs). A key challenge for next-generation implantable BCIs is to develop a spike detector with low hardware cost, high performance, and adaptive adjustment capabilities. In this work, we propose a novel hardware-efficient and high-performance spike detector for implantable BCIs. The proposed design is based on adaptive pre-emphasis and fixed threshold estimation. For adaptive pre-emphasis, a short-window convolutional filter is trained via an energy ratio loss function to enhance the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the signal.We evaluated the proposed spike detection algorithm on the Wave Clus dataset, achieving an average detection accuracy of 97.95%. Even in high-noise scenarios, the accuracy remains above 95%, which ensures the reliability of the method. The detector was implemented in hardware with a sampling rate of 24 kHz and a resolution of 8 bits. A multi-channel detector based on this architecture was designed using 65 nm process, exhibiting an area efficiency of 868 μm2per channel and a power consumption of 71.8 nW per channel.

title: TSA-P: A Triple-Sparsity-Aware Reconfigurable Few-Spikes-Neuron-Based SNN Processor.
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) hold great potential for energy-efficient computing by exploiting sparse, spike-driven processing. However, existing SNN processors directly adopt the zero-input/weight dual-sparsity scheme designed for Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs), neglecting the sparsity arising from repeated identical spike trains inherent in SNNs. This limitation, coupled with workload imbalance caused by unstructured pruning, constrains overall efficiency. To address these challenges, we propose TSA-P, a triple-sparsity-aware processor based on FSN-SNNs. In addition to dual-sparsity, we identify and exploit a third form of sparsity, termed Repetition Spike Train sparsity. To leverage these three sparsity forms, TSA-P introduces three key techniques—Adjacent Spike Train Compression (ASC) scheme, Spike-driven Weight Matching (SWM) method and Repeated Spike Train Reuse (RSR) strategy—which collectively minimize computational and memory-access energy. Furthermore, a hardware-friendly unstructured pruning (HUP) algorithm and a Sparsity-Adaptive Processing Element (SAPE) engine are developed to adaptively balance computational load while improving accuracy. TSA-P also features a reconfigurable architecture supporting both convolutional and fully connected layers. Experimental results on three datasets demonstrate that TSA-P achieves comparable accuracy while significantly reducing resource usage. On the CIFAR10 dataset, TSA-P achieves energy efficiency improvements ranging from 1.70× to 342.76× over state-of-the-art SNN processors.

title: A Logic-Assisted Hybrid-Mode Ising Machine Based on a 3D Topology for 3D Path Planning.
abstract: Path planning is a fundamental task in robotics, autonomous systems, and spatial optimization, in which real-time and energy-efficient computations are crucial. Conventional digital architectures exhibit limited parallelism when exploring large search spaces, leading to challenges in power efficiency, latency, and scalability. The Ising model offers a promising hardware framework for addressing such problems through energy-minimization dynamics. The spins that represent obstacles and paths in an Ising model update simultaneously, providing substantial acceleration in large-scale pathfinding. However, existing implementations are constrained by inefficient problem mapping and are typically limited to two-dimensional (2D) scenarios. To address these challenges, this work presents a CMOS Ising machine with a three-dimensional (3D) lattice topology for efficient 3D path planning, achieving a 91.3% reduction in transistor count compared with prior work. CMOS simulations verify that the proposed system correctly solves a 16 × 16 × 16 maze within 45 iterations, consuming 8.625 μW per spin and occupying 496.31 μm2per spin.

title: Exploring Structural and Behavioral Features for Hardware Trojan Detection at Gate Level.
abstract: Hardware Trojans are malicious design modifications to integrated circuit (IC) designs, which pose severe threats to hardware security and trust. This work proposes a novel hardware Trojan detection method at gate level by exploring structural and behavioral features and training a machine learning model for node classification. The gate-level netlist is converted into a directed graph to extract structural features for each node. A random forest algorithm is then employed to analyze feature importance, providing explainable insights into the most influential features. In addition, we transform the netlist to bench format and extract three behavioral features from the perspective of controllability and observability. A neural network model with optimized class-balanced focal loss is trained for classifying circuit nodes and identifying Trojan-infected ones. Experiments using 80 hardware Trojan benchmarks from Trust-Hub and ATTRITION show that the proposed method can successfully pinpoint Trojan-infected nodes with true positive rate (TPR), true negative rate (TNR), accuracy, and area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 99.46%, 96.56%, 96.57%, and 98.01% respectively on average.

title: Integrated Current and Vibration Sensing System for Condition Monitoring of a Drone Docking Station.
abstract: In this study, we present an integrated current and vibration sensing system designed to monitor drone docking station conditions using machine learning models for anomaly detection. The system also offers a plug-and-play monitoring capability with the potential to be adapted to various machinery. We developed two approaches: a long short-term memory (LSTM)-based classifier for known anomalies and an unsupervised convolutional neural network (CNN)-based autoencoder for detecting any deviations from normal operation. Validated on a real-world drone docking station, the reconstruction-based autoencoder, which does not require labeled data, achieves over 98.99% accuracy and a 98% F1-score.

title: CEDAR: A Compact and Efficient Decoder Architecture for RS-RM Code in HQC.
abstract: The rapid development of quantum computing has driven a new wave of cryptographic innovation: Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC), a class of algorithms that resist quantum attacks. In particular, the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has initiated the PQC standardization process, selecting five algorithms. Notably, HQC (the newest selection) is a code-based PQC scheme that has not been widely studied in the literature, especially with respect to its hardware acceleration. This paper follows the current trend to design CEDAR, a Compact and Efficient Decoder Architecture for Reed-Solomon Reed-Muller (RS-RM) code in HQC. We have proposed three layers of contributions in total: (i) an optimized RM decoder is designed; (ii) an efficient low-complexity RS decoder is also presented; (iii) a complete HQC decoder is implemented, along with a comprehensive evaluation (it is shown that CEDAR outperforms the existing approach). We hope this outcome will facilitate a more efficient hardware acceleration of HQC and impact the ongoing NIST PQC standardization process.

title: Closed-Loop Arrhythmia Classification with Level-Crossing Sensing and Bidirectional SNN.
abstract: This work proposes an event-driven sensing and inference framework that jointly optimizes signal acquisition and neural processing for energy-efficient, real-time Electrocardiography (ECG) analysis. Specifically, we present a closed-loop pipeline that integrates an adaptive Level-crossing Analog-to-digital Converter (LC-ADC) with a compact, fully spiking temporal back end. To validate hardware readiness, the complete signal path is implemented in Verilog RTL and synthesized in a 130 nm CMOS ASIC flow. The prototype attains 96.44% overall five-class classification accuracy and 98.02% detection accuracy on MIT–BIH dataset while consuming only 43 µW of average end-to-end power. These results are on par with recent state-of-the-art low-power arrhythmia detection systems, achieved with a lightweight (~50.3k parameter) Spiking Neural Network (SNN) and a simple ternary event interface. The combination of adaptive sensing and event-native inference makes the proposed design highly suitable for always-on, battery-constrained wearable healthcare devices.

title: A Highly-Scalable and Full-Connected SOT P-Bit Ising Annealer for Combinatorial Optimization.
abstract: Combinatorial optimization problems, which are fundamental to fields such as finance and artificial intelligence, remain challenging for classical computers due to their NP-hard nature. Ising machines have emerged as a promising physical platform that solves such problems by searching for the ground state of the Ising model. In this work, we propose an Ising machine implemented with spin-orbit torque probabilistic bits (SOT P-Bits). A scalable network of SOT MTJ-based P-Bits was constructed and a hardware-software co-calibration strategy was introduced to ensures behavioral consistency across probabilistic units. The compressed sparse row (CSR) method was applied to compress sparse weights while simultaneously optimizing the multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations. To mitigate the issue of local minima in large-scale instances, a local optimal temperature lifting (LOTL) method was employed during simulated annealing. The proposed Ising annealer comprises 1024 fully connected nodes, representing a scalable hardware implementation for solving large-scale combinatorial optimization problems. It has been experimentally evaluated and systematically verified across the device and system levels. The final results demonstrate that the system achieves significantly higher solution accuracy.

title: Live Demo of A Bidirectional Communication Gateway for Battery-free IoT End Devices.
abstract: A large-scale Internet of Things (IoT) system comprises numerous end devices [1] . To eliminate the inconvenience of wire arrangement and battery replacement, many previous studies have proposed battery-free (BF)-IoT end devices [2] . BF-IoT end devices integrate energy harvesting (EH) modules to capture ambient energy from sources including light, wind, radio-frequency (RF) signals, and human motion, and convert these energy forms into electrical power. This characteristic eliminates the requirement for conventional power cables or batteries. However, the energy output of EH modules is typically limited and volatile. Such energy constraints restrict the effective standby duration of BF-IoT end devices. As a result, most BF-IoT end devices cannot maintain continuous online status and are not directly compatible with energy-intensive wireless technologies (e.g., WiFi). This intermittent connectivity further indicates that traditional bidirectional communication—either between BF-IoT end devices and the host device or among different BF-IoT end devices—is not feasible. For this reason, most BF-IoT devices have not been supported by commercial smart home ecosystems (e.g., Google Assistant, Apple HomeKit, Xiaomi Mijia) to date.

title: A 210.6 nW FLL-based Standby Timer with Offset Compensation in 65nm CMOS for IoT Applications.
abstract: This work proposes a low-power, temperature-compensated frequency-to-voltage conversion (FVC)-based FLL as a standby timer for on-chip clock generation in compact and cost-constrained low-power IoT applications. The proposed architecture offers a viable crystal-alternative with high energy efficiency, incorporating inherent error amplifier offset cancellation and improved temperature stability compared to open-loop oscillators. A first-order RC low-pass filter inserted at the FVC feedback node effectively suppresses the ripple of the control voltage and output frequency FOUT, while comprehensive S-domain analysis verifies the loop stability. Fabricated in 65-nm CMOS, the FLL prototype generates a 2-MHz clock from a 0.6-V supply, consuming only 210.6 nW while achieving 80.2 ppm/^C stability across a temperature range of -30◦C to 70◦C. It demonstrates high energy efficiency with a figure of merit of 0.105 nW/kHz.

title: Dual Graph Feature Learning for ADHD Diagnosis: Integrating Node and Edge Information in Brain Networks.
abstract: Current graph neural network (GNN) approaches for analyzing brain functional connectivity networks (FCNs) in Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) often underutilize edge information and fail to capture dynamic node dependencies. To address these, we propose the Dual-Graph Feature Learning Network (DGFLN) for ADHD classification and biomarker discovery. Our framework constructs dual graph representations: a node graph, where multi-band amplitudes of low-frequency fluctuations (ALFF) serve as node features and both functional connectivity (FC) and node-wise relationships define edge attributes; and an edge graph derived through line graph theory, which facilitates the interchange of node and edge roles.DGFLN implements an alternating feature update mechanism with optimized graph convolution operations, facilitating hierarchical learning of node-edge relationships across network layers. Extensive experiments on the ADHD200 dataset achieve 97.3% accuracy, significantly outperforming existing methods. Additionally, gradient-based biomarker analysis identifies key regions in the bilateral limbic and default mode networks associated with ADHD, aligning with prior studies.

title: A Scalable and Highly Efficient NTT Unit for Crystals-Dilithium.
abstract: Dilithium was selected by NIST for its strong security, reliability, and quantum resistance. However, its large-scale polynomial multiplication relies on the Number Theoretic Transform (NTT), which remains a critical bottleneck. Efficient NTT/INTT implementations are thus vital for secure and reliable cryptographic circuits. Existing scenario-specific NTT designs achieve high performance but lack scalability, as their cycle counts and parallelism are fixed. To address this, we propose a configurable NTT/INTT unit for Dilithium supporting multiple parallelism levels. We optimize K-RED-based modular multiplication to reduce resource usage while maintaining a short critical path for higher frequencies. In addition, a conflict-free NTT architecture with two-dimensional processing elements (2D_PEs) is introduced to exploit stage parallelism, boosting throughput while lowering resources. The proposed design delivers efficient performance trade-offs and achieves 5.8%-82.5% area-time product (ATP) improvements over state-of-the-art FPGA works.

title: An Efficient Fully-Pipelined Hardware Architecture for Optimized Sparse Polynomial Multiplication in CRYSTALS-Dilithium.
abstract: Efficient hardware implementations for post-quantum cryptographic (PQC) algorithms are urgently needed for practical deployment. In this paper, we introduce a fully pipelined dual-input sparse polynomial multiplication architecture specifically optimized for CRYSTALS-Dilithium, a lattice-based digital signature algorithm selected by NIST. Our FPGA design fully exploits polynomial sparsity and a five-stage pipelined architecture, achieving significant improvements in computational performance and resource utilization. Experimental results on Xilinx Artix-7 and Virtex Ultrascale+ platforms demonstrate that the proposed sparse polynomial multiplication architecture achieves optimal hardware efficiency with fewer resources. Experimental data show approximately 2× speedup compared to existing state-of-the-art solutions, along with a 61.2% reduction in resource consumption. Thus, the proposed architecture provides an efficient and resource-optimized hardware implementation for sparse polynomial multiplication in CRYSTALS-Dilithium.

title: An Integrated Wearable Electromagnetic Sensing System with Wireless Vector Readout for Noninvasive Glucose Monitoring.
abstract: Noninvasive glucose monitoring is essential for diabetes management, yet current solutions either rely on invasive measurement or lack seamless integration for practical wearable use. This paper presents an integrated wearable electromagnetic (EM) sensing system with wireless vector readout for noninvasive glucose monitoring. The system consists of a nested-architecture metamaterial-inspired EM sensor and a compact stepped-frequency continuous-wave (SFCW) readout module. The two modules are vertically stacked to form a lightweight and skin-conformal sensing platform. The nested EM sensor generates weak omnidirectional electromagnetic coupling that increases sensing coverage and enhances sensitivity to glucose-induced permittivity variations. Furthermore, the wireless readout module performs real-time gain and phase demodulation, enabling vector sensing without the need for a benchtop vector network analyzer. In-vitro experiments across glucose concentrations from 0 to 400 mg/dL demonstrate clear monotonic trends in both amplitude and phase responses, confirming the effectiveness of the presented sensing system. Consequently, the proposed system offers a promising pathway toward practical wearable solutions for noninvasive continuous diabetes monitoring.

title: A Dual-Path SSHC Rectifier with Decoupled Battery Architecture for Enhanced Piezoelectric Energy Harvesting.
abstract: Piezoelectric energy harvesting is essential for enabling self-powered wireless sensor networks in Internet of Things applications. This paper presents the first analysis of the voltage-blocking mechanism in synchronized switch harvesting on capacitors (SSHC) rectifiers, which occurs when the piezoelectric voltage magnitude exceeds a threshold determined by the transducer’s impedance characteristics. This phenomenon occurs under shock excitation or low-frequency conditions, yet has been previously overlooked in capacitor-based rectification techniques. To address this limitation, a dual-path SSHC (DSSHC) architecture is proposed, employing two parallel energy extraction paths at different voltage levels to extend the energy harvesting window. The high-voltage path handles normal operation, while the low-voltage path maintains energy transfer during voltage-blocking conditions. A decoupled dual-battery architecture eliminates charge redistribution losses between storage capacitors. Simulation results using an 8-stage implementation demonstrate 4.92% higher peak output power compared to conventional SSHC and elimination of voltage-blocking conditions.

title: SCOPE-3D: An Energy Efficient Accelerator for Implicit Neural Representation-based Sparse-view Computed Tomography Reconstruction.
abstract: The increasing demand for portable CT and other resource-constrained clinical environments necessitates compact and low-power reconstruction systems. This paper presents 3D Self-supervised Coordinate Projection (SCOPE-3D), a low-power hardware-efficient accelerator for Sparse-View Computed Tomography (SVCT) based on Implicit Neural Representation (INR), an emerging paradigm in reconstruction. The SCOPE-3D architecture is optimized for the computational flow of our proposed INR-based SVCT reconstruction algorithm, integrating a hash encoding module, fully connected network computation arrays, and a ray accumulation module. Fabricated in a 40nm CMOS process, the SCOPE-3D chip occupies a total area of 5.74 mm2, operates at frequencies ranging from 55.6 MHz to 166.7 MHz, and consumes between 16.8 mW and 61.0 mW of power. SCOPE-3D represents a promising solution for energy-efficient SVCT rendering in embedded medical imaging systems.

title: Cryogenic Influences on Frequency Dividers and Output Buffers in Ring-Oscillator Design and Characterization.
abstract: Qubit-interfacing circuit design at 4 K is critical to system performance in many quantum-computing platforms. Cryogenic influences in silicon processes, combined with stringent power budgets, impede specification-compliant CMOS integrated circuit design at 4 K, motivating a departure from conventional design approaches. This work targets key building blocks of frequency-reference chains within qubit controllers, including ring oscillators, frequency dividers, and output buffers. Two comparable designs were implemented in a 65-nm process: a baseline standard-cell design and a 4-K-optimized custom design. Their performance is compared in terms of supply current, output frequency, and rms period jitter. Measurement results demonstrate that the non-ideal cryogenic effects observed in the standard-cell design can be mitigated through the use of low threshold voltage CMOS, comprehensive guard-ring layouts, and a simplified D-latch design. These customizations yield thermally stable frequency performance while reducing power dissipation by approximately 20 times and rms period jitter by over 19 times at sub-4 K. This work characterizes the cryogenic manifestations in standard-cell implementations and demonstrates their mitigation via a custom design, serving as a practical reference for future cryogenic CMOS developments.

title: A Low-Power FPGA Implementation of QRS Detection for Real-Time Heart Rate Monitoring.
abstract: Wearable heart rate monitoring relies on efficient QRS detection for real-time ECG analysis, yet traditional algorithms demand high computational resources, making them unsuitable for low-power platforms. We present an optimized FPGA implementation of a QRS detection algorithm using adaptive thresholding and parallel processing, achieving millijoule-level energy consumption and over 98.5% accuracy on several widely used real-world ECG datasets. The design leverages fixed-point arithmetic and a pipelined architecture to minimize latency (under 5 ms) and resource utilization (under 35% of LUTs on a Zynq-7020). Compared to software-based counterparts, our implementation achieves a 7.8–43.0× improvement in power efficiency, while maintaining clinical-grade precision, enabling operation in battery-powered wearable monitoring devices.

title: Transient Stability Prediction for AC Microgrids Using a Data-Driven Approach.
abstract: Transient stability assessment (TSA) is paramount for ensuring the reliability of AC microgrids comprising both grid-forming (GFM) and grid-following (GFL) converters, especially in multi-machine systems subjected to large disturbances. Conventional methods including time-domain simulations, manifold-based bifurcation analysis, and the Lyapunov energy function approach, are often hampered by computational inefficiency, model complexity, or excessive conservatism. These limitations render them unsuitable for the rapid stability evaluation required in modern power electronics-dominated grids. To overcome these challenges, this paper introduces a novel data-driven framework for fast and accurate transient stability prediction. Leveraging machine learning (ML) techniques, this paper proposes a data-driven method, which bypasses the need for computationally expensive simulations and analytical approximations. The results demonstrate that our framework significantly reduces computational burden while maintaining high predictive accuracy, facilitating near real-time assessment. This work provides a practical and scalable solution for enhancing transient stability management in inverter-based AC microgrids.

title: Layer-Aware Timing-Driven Global Routing for Advanced Technology Nodes.
abstract: Routing is a critical stage for VLSI timing closure. Global routing algorithms without considering timing delay might lead to inferior solutions with timing violations. This paper proposes a timing-driven global router for advanced technology nodes. First, we present a congestion-aware layer planning method that assigns an optimal routing layer range for each critical net. Then, we design a timing-driven Steiner tree construction algorithm that generates a timing-optimal topology through a Single-Source Shortest Path (SSSP) based reconstruction. Finally, we develop a timing-constrained multi-level maze router to resolve congestion without timing degradation. Experimental results on 7nm industrial benchmarks show that, compared to an advanced commercial tool and the leading academic engine OpenROAD, our proposed routing algorithm achieves the best results on key timing metrics (WNS and TNS).

title: Layout-Aware Standard Cell Synthesis via Reparameterization Multi-Task Bayesian Optimization.
abstract: Standard cells (SCs) fundamentally influence the power, performance, and area (PPA) of digital integrated circuits. With advances in manufacturing technology and increasing integration density, traditional sequential design flows face two challenges: upstream "optimal designs" diverge from post-layout reality, and isolated design stages restrict the solution space. We introduce LASS, a Layout-Aware Standard Cell Synthesis framework. LASS addresses key challenges through (1) a multitask Gaussian process(MTGP) regression model that captures the correlation between pre- and post-layout simulation1results to transfer rich pre-layout data and enhance post-layout modeling under limited data; and (2) a reparameterization-based probabilistic improvement (RePI) acquisition function for efficient exploration in discontinuous design spaces. Experimental results show that LASS optimizes the PPA figure-of-merit (FoM) to 78% in the best case and 84% on average, compared to the X1-driven designs. Moreover, case studies confirm tangible circuit-level performance improvements, with up to 35% delay reduction.

title: Precise Hardware Trojan Localization at RTL Through Graph-Based Feature Integration.
abstract: Under a globalized semiconductor supply chain, hardware Trojans have become a significant threat to hardware security and trustworthiness. In this work, we propose a novel hardware Trojan localization method at register transfer level (RTL) using graph convolutional networks (GCNs). We integrate both static circuit structural features extracted from RTL code and dynamic behavioral features obtained through random simulation to form comprehensive node-level representations. A four-layer GCN model is then trained for classifying design nodes in RTL code and identifying the Trojan-infected ones, in which class-balanced (CB) focal loss is employed to effectively address the class imbalance issue. Experimental results using 42 RTL benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed method can successfully locate Trojan-infected nodes in hardware designs with true positive rate (TPR), true negative rate (TNR), accuracy and area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 94.72%, 97.01%, 97.00% and 97.83% respectively on average.

title: An Efficient BIST and Fault Diagnosis Circuit for TSVs.
abstract: 3D integrated circuits incorporate a high density of die-to-die(D2D) interconnects to enable functional connectivity between chiplets. The bonding process for these high-density interconnects is susceptible to manufacturing defects, which can induce various interconnect faults. To effectively test various faults, test algorithms and built-in self-test (BIST) techniques based on the Kth-aggressor fault (KAF) model are employed, but also prolong the test duration, elevates overall chip testing costs. To address this issue, this paper propose a test and diagnosis pattern generation algorithm utilizing true/complement codes. The proposed algorithm is fully compatible with the KAF model, covers ten fault types between any two inter-group TSVs, and enables concurrent fault localization and diagnosis. Furthermore, we design a BIST circuit featuring time-division multiplexing diagnosis logic, implemented based on the proposed algorithm. Compared to the current fastest scheme, the proposed method reduces the test time by approximately 10.2% for a given group of TSV interconnects.

title: A Low-phase-error FD-fNIRS Readout Circuit with Sub-1V Transimpedance Amplifier and LC-ADC-based Amplitude Control Loop.
abstract: Frequency-domain functional near-infrared spectroscopy (FD-fNIRS) ultilizes the propagation time and amplitude attenuation of light in tissue to quantify blood oxygen concentration. This enables more detailed monitoring of human brain activity, providing a potential solution for non-invasive and wearable brain-computer interface (BCI) devices. However, the amplitude-phase coupling effect of the comparator in the phase detector introduces phase errors, which in turn leads to inaccuracies in the measurement of light propagation time. To suppress amplitude-phase coupling effect, an amplitude control loop based on the level-crossing analog-to-digital converter (LC ADC) is employed. The utilization of the LC ADC eliminates the need for a high-speed envelope detector, thereby reducing circuit complexity and power consumption. In addition, a sub-1V transimpedance amplifier (TIA) is employed to improve energy efficiency. The proposed structure achieves a phase error of 0.11° and 12 mW power consumption.

title: Lightweight Quadrupolar Trapezoidal Coil Design with CNN-Accelerated Optimization for Misalignment-Tolerant IPT Converter.
abstract: Inductive Power Transfer (IPT) has become a pivotal technology for various applications. While diverse enhancement strategies have been explored, the magnetically coupled coil remains the ultimate determinant of system performance. Horizontal coil misalignment is particularly critical, causing coupling variations that destabilize output and degrade efficiency. Current solutions are either bulky compensation networks or complex multilayered coil geometries with limited scalability. This paper proposes a lightweight, misalignment-tolerance coil structure that merges quadrupolar trapezoidal transmit coils with a unipolar square receive coil, inherently flattening mutual-inductance variation across ±50% horizontal misalignment. To overcome time-consuming finite element analysis, we also develop a convolutional neural network (CNN) regression-prediction framework trained on multi-physics datasets, reducing design time by two orders of magnitude while preserving scalability and reusability. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed CNN-based framework’s exceptional accuracy across all statistical metrics (R2, RMSE, MAE, MBE). Furthermore, the optimized prototype exhibits only 2.65 % mutual-inductance fluctuation within the targeted misalignment range.

title: Performance-Aware Design Space Exploration for Chiplet-Based Cortical Simulation Processors Considering Area Constraint.
abstract: Cortical simulation is limited by memory capacity and I/O bandwidth due to massive neuron counts, large fan-out, and sparse irregular connectivity. To address these constraints under a fixed total area budget, we adopt a chiplet-based solution in which a compute die is co-packaged with multiple HBM stacks on an interposer to form a tile, and many tiles are interconnected on wafer. A central question is the tile size: larger tiles concentrate more compute and SRAM but, for a fixed total area, reduce the total number of I/O lanes in the system and thus lower aggregate off-chip memory and inter-chip bandwidth; smaller tiles improve modularity and yield and increase total I/O, but raise inter-chip traffic and hop count. Motivated by this trade-off, we present a performance-aware architecture and physical co-optimization framework that explores the key design parameters. We model cortical simulation performance as the pipeline maximum of three stages: neural dynamics computing, spike routing, and synaptic information access. The framework evaluates a compact set of configurations that vary tile count, HBM stacks per tile, and the I/O split, and applies a temporal equalization principle that balances routing and synaptic access latencies. For a cortical model with 800,000 neurons, the method identifies an optimal configuration under the given constraints, achieving a 2.42× performance improvement over the average of all feasible configurations.

title: Energy Efficient Vector Gather Based on Data Serialization and Pulse Selection.
abstract: To address the issue of hardware overhead sharply increasing with vector bit width in traditional implementations of vector gather instructions, this paper proposes a hardware architecture based on time-domain computation. This architecture achieves a transition from the digital domain to the time domain through the coordinated operation of five modules: index vector extraction, delay chain, pulse selection, data serialization, and vector sampling. It serializes the transmission of source vectors via pulse timing encoding and performs synchronous sampling using index-driven pulses to complete vector gather. Test results from logic synthesis and circuit simulation on a 28nm process node demonstrate that compared to the baseline circuit, this architecture lowers power consumption by 71.3% and saves 33.1% in area. Furthermore, as vector width increases, both power consumption and area growth of this architecture remain lower than the baseline design, showcasing excellent application potential for scenarios requiring higher bit widths or constrained hardware resources.

title: A Low-Power Resonate-and-Fire Neuron with Adaptive Refractory Control for RRAM-Based Neuromorphic Computing.
abstract: Traditional Spiking Neural Network (SNN) models, such as the Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) neuron, lack intrinsic resonance behaviors required for effective temporal and sequential processing. More complex models offer better biological realism but are often hardware-inefficient when implemented digitally. This paper presents a low-power Modified Balanced Resonate-and-Fire (MB-RAF) neuron with adaptive refractory control, derived from the Lotka–Volterra dynamic system. The proposed design incorporates two tunable parameters: ω, which modulates the oscillation frequency, and β, which regulates leakage. An adaptive refractory mechanism dynamically adjusts the threshold to enhance sparsity and prevent excessive firing. Implemented in 55 nm CMOS technology, the proposed MB-RAF neuron achieves ultra-low power consumption, with 25.29 µW during firing and 23.81 µW during hibernation. It is integrated with a 1024 × 128 RRAM synaptic array to form a functional hardware SNN system, demonstrating high classification accuracies on S-mnist, SHD and ECG datasets. These results highlight the MB-RAF neuron’s strong potential for compact and energy-efficient neuromorphic computing applications.

abstract: This article presents a generic reliable Cryo-VLSI design flow platform aimed at optimizing CMOS performance for efficient high-performance computing at cryogenic temperatures. title: A 1.2-3.4 Gb/s Low-Power Multiphase CDR with Glitch-Free Bang-Bang Phase Detector.
abstract: This paper presents a multiphase clock and data recovery (CDR) circuit for high-speed (1.2-3.4 Gb/s) display driver ICs (DDIs) with a novel glitch-free bang-bang phase detector (BBPD). Compared to conventional BBPDs, which often suffer from sampling glitches caused by latch-delay mismatches and asynchronous data-edge interferences, the proposed BBPD employs a robust sampling network ensuring mutually exclusive data-edge valid events, thereby filtering invalid transitions and minimizing timing-induced jitter. An extensive comparison with conventional BBPDs highlights these improvements and clarifies how the proposed BBPD enhances phase detection integrity and overall stability in high-speed CDRs. Fabricated in a 0.18-μm CMOS process and integrated in a chip-on-film (COF) package along with other DDI's components, the proposed CDR demonstrates a clean output phase trajectory and an improved 97 ps output jitter (0.388 UI at 4 Gb/s) with only 20.1 mW power consumption including the equalizer power. title: A 0.036mm2 Cross-Coupled Class-AB High-Voltage Amplifier with Unipolar/Bipolar Output Using 180nm BCD for Multi-Channel MEMS Drivers.
abstract: This paper presents a cross-coupled push–pull Class-AB high-voltage amplifier (HV-AMP) tailored for multi-channel MEMS driver applications. Conventional charge-pump or stacked-MOSFET approaches often introduce voltage ripple, large device overhead, and limited ability to realize both unipolar and bipolar outputs. By contrast, the proposed cross-coupled push–pull Class-AB architecture uses only six laterally diffused metal-oxide-semiconductor (LDMOS) devices to enable rail-to-rail high-voltage operation, while maintaining linear amplifier performance. This design supports reconfigurable output ranges, providing either unipolar 0–30V or bipolar ±15V output without additional biasing circuits. Implemented in a 180nm BCD process, this design occupies 0.036mm2and achieves an 85dB low-frequency gain, a 1MHz gain–bandwidth, and a 97.65V/µs slew rate. The amplifier consumes 0.65mW in unipolar mode and bipolar mode, demonstrating both high efficiency and compact area. These features make the proposed HV-AMP a promising building block for scalable, low-power, and high slew rate MEMS driver arrays.

title: Edge-RamanSBL-Net: Compressed Sensing-Based Real-Time Directional Raman Qualitative Unmixing via Network Unfolding and One-Shot Training.
abstract: Raman spectroscopy enables accurate substance identification by leveraging its inherent fingerprint characteristics, yet edge-side Raman spectral qualitative unmixing analysis faces two critical challenges: traditional methods suffer from low inference efficiency and high resource consumption, while deep learning-based methods rely heavily on large-scale labeled data. So this paper proposes a Sparse Bayesian Learning (SBL) unfolded network named Edge-RamanSBL-Net (ERSN) to address the pain points. ERSN adopts a cascaded unfolded architecture with 5 SBL layers, converting the iterative optimization of SBL into the forward network to learn the mapping relationship between mxiture spectra and multiple pure components and support high-dimensional dictionary input. Through a network parameter sharing mechanism, the model weight is compressed to 6.13MB. During the training phase, a hierarchical decrement strategy is employed to decouple training sufficiency from testing flexibility, allowing inference complexity to be adjusted on demand. Experiments validated with data collected by portable instruments show that on 16 types of mixture samples (10 spectra per type), both the positive identification rate and recall rate reach 100%, with an average execution time of 40ms per spectrum (75-fold speedup). Moreover, only one 5-component mixture spectrum is required to complete One-Shot training. ERSN is an effective solution for fast and accurate Raman qualitative unmixing on edge devices.

The system captures subtle foot movements in all directions and fine pressure variations from toe contacts. title: InFP: A 17.97 TFLOPS/W Reconfigurable SRAM Based Computing-in-Memory Macro for BF16 MAC Operations.
abstract: As the demand for high-precision training and inference of deep neural networks (DNNs) continues to grow, floating-point (FP) compute-in-memory (CIM) architecture has emerged as an essential solution. However, in contrast to extensively studied integer (INT) CIM, the efficiency of FP-CIM still requires further enhancement. In this paper, we present an energy-efficient and area-efficient digital SRAM-based FP-CIM macro with reconfigurable peripheral logic. Specifically, we design an interleaved SRAM bank with specific weight mapping, which improves SRAM utilization and enables write-compute pipeline scheduling to maximize hardware usage. Additionally, to improve energy efficiency and reduce area requirements, we propose a reconfigurable peripheral logic equipped with a shared addition unit, conducting exponent and mantissa addition at different stages of the FP MAC operation. A 16kb SRAM CIM macro with the proposed techniques is designed in TSMC 45nm CMOS technology and occupies an area of 0.081 mm2. The simulation results show that our work achieves a peak energy efficiency of 17.97 TFLOPS/W and an area efficiency of 0.395 TFLOPS/mm2with brain-float 16 (BF16) representation.

title: Physics-guided AI-Assisted Modeling of Flexible Transistors Based on Fully-Additive Printed Electronics Process.
abstract: Fully-additive printed electronics enables low-cost and flexible circuit fabrication, but severe process variations significantly degrade device uniformity and modeling accuracy. This work presents an AI-assisted modeling framework for flexible thin-film transistors (TFTs) fabricated via a fully-additive printed electronics process. To accurately capture the nonlinear current voltage characteristics of the printed transistors, a hybrid AI-assisted model is proposed, combining a physics-based trend equation with a residual neural network (RNN). The trend model provides a physically interpretable baseline describing the device’s general behavior, while the RNN learns the fine-grained residuals from experimental data. A physics-informed loss function is further incorporated to enforce smoothness and monotonicity, ensuring that the model adheres to fundamental device physics. Experimental validation on printed flexible FETs demonstrates that the proposed approach achieves high prediction accuracy and physical consistency across wide bias ranges and different bending conditions.

title: SVVHD: An Open-Source and Self-Verified Benchmark Framework for LLM Evaluation in VHDL Code Generation.
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate significant potential for generating and verifying Hardware Description Languages (HDLs) in Electronic Design Automation. However, a notable gap exists in VHDL code generation compared to other HDLs, exacerbated by the absence of an open-source benchmark. To address this gap, we propose SVVHD, an open-source benchmark for evaluating LLMs on VHDL code generation. The first part of SVVHD is an evaluation dataset, constructed by translating 156 diverse Verilog problems into VHDL, employing prompt refactoring and rigorous code equivalence verification. The second part of SVVHD is a set of automated testbenches that perform functional verification of candidate VHDL designs against golden solutions within a sandbox environment. Using SVVHD, we conduct zero-shot code generation evaluations with various LLMs to establish baseline performance for the VHDL code generation domain. Subsequently, we construct both a refactored training set and a basic training set for model fine-tuning, which yield significant performance improvements. The introduction of SVVHD, combined with our fine-tuning methodology, contributes to advancing research in LLM-assisted automated VHDL design.

title: A High-PSRR Pitch-Matched Ultrasound Receiver Analog Front-End with Integrated Beamforming for PMUT-Based Ultrasound Imaging.
abstract: This paper presents a high-PSRR pitch-matched ultrasound receiver analog front-end (AFE) circuit for miniaturized ultrasound imaging system based-on piezoelectric micromachined ultrasound transducer (PMUT). The AFE is designed to receive echo signals from a 9-channel 2-D PMUT array. The 9-channel AFE integrates nine low-noise amplifiers (LNAs), an analog beamforming (BF) circuit, and a programmable gain amplifier (PGA) within the 200-μm pitch channel while achieving high-PSRR and consuming low-power. A compact current-reused LNA is adopted to achieve pitch-matching. However, its power supply rejection ratio (PSRR) is inherently poor, especially in closely integrated pitch-matched AFE. To address this challenge, a high-PSRR channel-shared low-dropout regulator (LDO) is employed to power nine LNAs. The proposed LDO introduces a pre-LDO stage, significantly improving PSRR while reducing power consumption. The BF is implemented by pipelined sample-and-hold scheme to delay and sum the outputs of nine LNAs, reducing the number of PGAs. The PGA with adjustable gains of 6/12/18/24 dB implements time gain compensation. The proposed 9-channel AFE is designed in a 180nm CMOS process with a compact area of 0.0141 mm2/channel, achieving an input-referred noise of 4.08nV/√Hz@3MHz. a PSRR of 76.8dB@3MHz, and an average power consumption of 0.476 mW/channel.

title: FRRAP: A Fast-Response Reconfigurable AI Processor and Its Application in Four-Class Seizure Monitoring.
abstract: Human medical signal processing systems face significant challenges in clinical deployment, including stringent real-time constraints, limited hardware efficiency, and poor generalization. This paper presents a fast-response reconfigurable artificial intelligence processor (FRRAP) based on a coarse-grained reconfigurable architecture (CGRA), specifically designed for low-latency and energy-efficient biomedical signal processing. To validate the proposed architecture, seizure monitoring is selected as a representative application requiring minimal latency. We proposed a four-class seizure monitoring model that integrates both seizure prediction and detection functions, leveraging a task decomposition algorithm to mitigate class imbalance in the training data. The model employs a shared dual-branch neural network, achieving a classification accuracy of 94.07% on the CHB-MIT dataset with only 10.26 K parameters. Fabricated in 12 nm CMOS technology, FRRAP incorporates multi-level configuration mechanisms and dynamic instruction prefetching to enhance execution efficiency. The system achieves a seizure detection latency of 0.61 s, representing a 39% improvement over conventional ASIC-based accelerators. Enabled by a large-scale array of processing elements and on-chip memory, FRRAP supports a wide range of high-throughput medical signal processing workloads, offering the flexibility and scalability to accommodate emerging applications in real-time health monitoring and beyond.

title: Asymmetric Read Transistor Configuration Enabled Low-Power 2T0C CAA-AOSFET Crossbar Array through Sneak Current Suppression.
abstract: The three-dimensional stacked two-transistor capacitor-less (2T0C) memory architecture based on channel-all-around amorphous oxide semiconductor field-effect transistors (CAA-AOSFETs) is a promising candidate to overcome the capacitor scaling bottleneck in future high-density DRAM. Although the decoupled read/write path of the 2T0C cell enables read operations at voltages as low as 0.1 V, its low-power potential in large-scale arrays has not been systematically investigated. This work analyzes sneak current impact on read margin and power in a 2T0C crossbar. Compared to 1T1C DRAM, 2T0C reduces read energy by 50% by eliminating restore and lowering precharge energy, yet sneak current becomes dominant. To address this, we propose and validate an asymmetric read transistor electrode configuration (AsymTEC) to suppress sneak currents at the array level. Measurement results demonstrate that in a 512-cell read bit line (RBL), a read transistor with a 0.2 V bidirectional threshold voltage difference reduces sneak current by over 80%, enabling a 4 ns RBL pull-down time at a 0.7 V read array supply voltage.

title: A Pipelined NoC-Based Membrane Shortcut SNN Architecture for Low-Latency Spike Sorting.
abstract: Spike sorting, a fundamental process in brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), necessitates increasingly high-throughput, low-latency, and energy-efficient computing paradigm. Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) have emerged as promising candidates owing to their event-driven and low-power nature. However, the hardware performance of advanced architectures like residual SNNs is severely hindered by a long-standing challenge: the lack of an efficient multi-core communication mechanism for their critical residual connections. To bridge this gap, we propose PMS-NoC, a Pipeline Membrane Shortcut Network-on-Chip architecture that, for the first time, optimizes membrane shortcut SNN data flow on multi-core neuromorphic hardware. We introduce two key strategies: a dual-packet time-division multiplexing strategy that significantly improves pipeline efficiency, reducing spike sorting inference time by 29.37%, and a distributed multi-core pipeline synchronization strategy minimizing parallel computation errors and improving inference accuracy by 11.7%. Our FPGA prototype of PMS-NoC, utilizing a mesh router for compressed 16-bit packets, achieves high throughput of 817.9 K timesteps per second at 3.3 μs latency. This work provides a feasible and efficient hardware framework, paving the way for the deployment of advanced residual SNNs in real-time BCI systems.

title: A Power Efficient and Fast Response Cascode FVF LDO Using Voltage Detecting and GB Enhancing Techniques for Cryogenic Quantum Computing.
abstract: This paper presents a low power consumption, high current efficiency and fast response low-dropout voltage regulator (LDO) without external capacitors (capless) working at cryogenic temperature (4K). The flipped-voltage-follower (FVF) structure achieves large bandwidth with low power consumption. The voltage detecting unit provides not only extra current but also low voltage overshoot and undershoot when the load steps. The gain bandwidth (GB) enhancing structure with active inductors is adopted to improve loop bandwidth to realize better transient response. The proposed LDO is fabricated in a 28-nm CMOS process, occupying only 0.0026mm2. Measured results show that the LDO provides a voltage of 0.9V and a quiescent current of 15.1μA achieving current efficiency of 99.94 % and loading 25mA at 4K. It achieves 48mV undershoot and 45mV overshoot with a step of 24.95mA/10ns. The results show that the LDO can power circuits at cryogenic temperature and can be applied to large-scale quantum computers.

title: MA-RQAOA: A System-Algorithm Co-Design Framework for Coherence-Limited Topological Quantum Computing.
abstract: Topological quantum computing (TQC) with Majorana zero modes (MZMs) promises scalable, fault-tolerant computation, but is severely constrained by finite coherence times (1ms) and costly non-Clifford gates. Standard hybrid algorithms like the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) are hardware-agnostic and often produce physically unrealizable solutions. To address this, we introduce the Majorana-Aware Recursive QAOA (MA-RQAOA), a system-algorithm co-design framework. MA-RQAOA embeds a hardware-aware temporal cost model directly into its classical optimization loop, formulating the task as a constrained variational search. This guarantees that the discovered quantum circuits are executable within the processor's coherence time. Through simulations on Max-Cut problems, we demonstrate that MA-RQAOA consistently identifies high-quality, feasible solutions, significantly outperforming standard approaches that are frequently invalidated by hardware constraints. Our work presents a new paradigm for developing practical quantum algorithms that are deeply integrated with the realities of physical hardware.

title: DNA-HHE: Dual-mode Near-network Accelerator for Hybrid Homomorphic Encryption on the Edge.
abstract: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) schemes (e.g., RNS-CKKS) support Privacy-Preserving Outsourced Computation (PPOC) yet face high computational latency and ciphertext expansion, especially on resource-constrained edge devices. Hybrid Homomorphic Encryption (HHE) alleviates these edge issues by using lightweight symmetric encryption (e.g., Rubato cipher for RNS-CKKS-based HHE) instead of HE for plaintext encryption, but introduces transciphering overhead on the cloud. This trade-off demands a flexible dual-mode solution. This paper presents DNA-HHE, to our knowledge the first dual-mode HHE accelerator with near-network coupling capability for edge devices. DNA-HHE unifies RNS-CKKS and Rubato support, driven by flexible instructions. For compact edge deployment, we propose three key designs: DSP-efficient modular reduction, compact multi-field-adaptive butterfly unit, and Rubato parallel scheduling with high resource sharing. Crucially, DNA-HHE is directly coupled to the NIC, handling network protocol packaging to reduce end-to-end PPOC latency by 1.09× to 1.56×. ASIC and FPGA evaluations show DNA-HHE outperforms state-of-the-art single-mode designs in both latency and area efficiency, while providing this critical dual-mode functionality.

title: An Ultra-Low Quiescent Current Step-down DC-DC Converter for Heavy Load Automotive Applications.
abstract: DC-DC converters are broadly used in automotive systems where specifications such as quiescent current (IQ), efficiency, electromagnetic interference (EMI) and so forth are critical for system performance. In this work, we propose a peak current mode (PCM) DC-DC converter that combines low EMI performance together with ultra-low IQin light load conditions. An innovative frequency modulation method based on a voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) using the output of the error amplifier is proposed to achieve smooth transition from pulse-width modulation in heavy load with fixed switching frequency to pulse-frequency modulation in light load. A green mode control architecture is introduced to shutdown most of the active circuits so that minimal IQis required to maintain regulation when load is light to prolong battery life. The converter was designed and fabricated on a 180-nm BCD process with 4.4 mm2die area and flip-chip copper pillar package is employed to further reduce the EMI noise. The fabricated chip supports load current up to 10A and consumes as low as 3.8μA IQunder no load conditions, making it suitable for automotive applications.

title: An Artifact-Suppressing Neural Stimulator Using Differential Push-Pull Architecture.
abstract: This paper presents a neural stimulator that suppresses stimulus artifacts for closed-loop brain-machine interfaces. The proposed differential push-pull architecture leverages dual stimulation sources to realize artifacts cancellation at the recording site. Fabricated in a 180nm BCD process, the chip integrates timing logic, current-steering digital-to-analog converters, and high-voltage drivers— enabling the stimulator to achieve a voltage compliance of 20 V. Simulation results show the design can reduce the peak-to-peak artifact voltage from 1.2 V to 180 mV, which equals to 85% suppression. This enables robust simultaneous stimulation and recording.

title: FPGA-Accelerated Real-Time Image Reconstruction For CMOS Electrochemical Sensing Arrays.
abstract: This paper presents a real-time, high-speed decompression and image reconstruction platform for Ion-Sensitive Field-Effect Transistor (ISFET) arrays, implemented on FPGA. The system leverages compressed sensing (CS) principles and employs an Iterative Hard Thresholding (IHT) algorithm to reconstruct ISFET images from highly compressed measurements in real time. The hardware implementation reconstructs a 32×32 ISFET image from a compressed signal with a compression ratio of 4:1, achieving a peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of up to 27.49 dB. The reconstruction latency from the compressed signal input buffer to the output image buffer is 870 μs. The FPGA-based platform integrates a real-time readout and control interface for the ISFET array, along with a user-friendly visualisation interface that displays the reconstructed images dynamically. The platform constitutes a portable and energy-efficient solution for the ISFET System-on-Chip (SoC) enhanced with compressed sensing. It enables configurable image processing parameters to accommodate a range of image sensing applications.

title: A Low Power Current Sensor with 84.6dB SNR for Battery Management System.
abstract: A low-power, low-offset sigma–delta modulator (ΣΔM) based current sensor for battery management systems (BMS) is presented in this work. The impact of offset and low-frequency noise of OTA on ΣΔM performance is analyzed, motivating the adoption of multi-level chopping techniques for precision enhancement. An integrated amplifier-chopping circuit is embedded within the OTA to suppress DC offset and 1/f noise, while an additional system-level chopping scheme further minimizes residual offset and enhances overall accuracy. The modulator employs a third-order feedforward architecture to achieve higher resolution than conventional second-order designs. Fabricated using a 0.18-μm BCD process, the prototype achieves a peak signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 84.6 dB with a total power consumption of only 130 μA, demonstrating its effectiveness for high-precision, low-power current sensing in BMS applications.

title: Sensitivity Analysis of Process Variables for Large-Scale Circuits based on Graph Attention Networks.
abstract: Process variations in advanced semiconductor technologies pose significant challenges to circuit reliability and yield, making process-variable sensitivity analysis (SA) essential. However, traditional SA methods suffer from prohibitive computational costs or insufficient accuracy, especially for large-scale circuits. In this paper, we propose a novel and scalable process-variable SA framework based on Graph Attention Network (GAT). Our key idea is to convert the circuit into a graph and train a GAT-based model to learn the complex, nonlinear mapping between process variables and circuit performance. To further enhance the scalability of our method, we introduce virtual nodes into the graph based on circuit hierarchy to improve interaction between long-range nodes in large-scale circuits. Sensitivities can be calculated using the gradient of the model’s output with respect to its inputs. Experiments on an 8-bit population counter and a 4-word-2-bit SRAM array demonstrate that our proposed method is effective in identifying critical process variables.

title: CircuitS2L: Circuit Dataset Augmentation via Generative Featuring and Supervised Labeling.
abstract: Learning-based techniques are increasingly integrated into electronic design automation (EDA) tool to accelerate and improve the design process. Yet, their success depends on large, diverse circuit datasets, which are scarce due to strict data privacy and confidentiality in the semiconductor industry. To address this challenge, we propose CircuitS2L, a data augmentation framework that enables task-aware generative feature augmentation for both tabular and graph-structured circuit data, producing richer and more diverse representations. CircuitS2L also introduces a supervised label generation strategy that remains robust under limited data by training in an interpretable and task-consistent manner. This ensures that the generated features and labels align with representative downstream EDA tasks, enhancing model performance and generalizability. Evaluations across multiple downstream prediction tasks show that CircuitS2L-augmented data significantly improves prediction results, achieving up to 64% MAE reduction compared to real data alone in LLM-based downstream tasks.

title: A Configurable Energy-Efficient Dual-Mode Accelerator for DNN and SNN.
abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) have achieved remarkable success in various applications but incur high power consumption due to intensive multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations. Inspired by biological neurons, spiking neural networks (SNNs) provide an energy-efficient alternative through sparse, event-driven computation. Although dedicated SNN accelerators demonstrate superior energy efficiency, they still lag behind DNNs in accuracy and computational performance. Notably, since the MAC operations in DNNs are highly similar to the synaptic integration in SNNs, a unified accelerator can efficiently support both types of networks with minimal additional hardware overhead. Motivated by this observation, this work proposed a configurable dual-mode accelerator built on a unified weight-stationary systolic array that efficiently supports both DNNs and SNNs by performing dense and spike matrix vector multiplication (GEMV) and matrix matrix matrix multiplication (GEMM) operations, maximizing hardware reuse. Implemented in TSMC 28 nm CMOS technology at a frequency of 500 MHz, the accelerator achieves energy efficiencies of 9.75 TOPS/W and 9.75 TSOPS/W for DNN and SNN workloads, respectively. Compared with existing accelerators, this corresponds to 1.9× and 2.7× the energy efficiency of previous DNN and SNN designs.

title: Energy-Efficiency Monitoring and Parallel Fault Protection BMIC for Battery Management.
abstract: This paper presents a battery-pack monitoring and protection IC (BMIC) that achieves low power consumption and high detection accuracy for battery management systems (BMS). Conventional designs suffer from sensing latency and offset accumulation, motivating a dual-path high-voltage multiplexer with an auxiliary drive structure that ensures switch cascadability and sampling precision under disordered power-up conditions. A parallel-synchronous architecture is further proposed, enabling cooperative voltage acquisition and protection decision-making through time-division multiplexed control. The BMIC supports monitoring and protection for 16 series-connected cells, featuring configurable overvoltage, undervoltage, and overcurrent protection. Fabricated in 180-nm BCD, the prototype achieves a detection error below 5 mV and operates at 294 μA, demonstrating its effectiveness for low-power, high-reliability BMS applications.

title: A Constant-Loss 6.78-MHz Wireless Power Transfer System with Hybrid Class-ED Power Amplifier for D2D Fast Charging.
abstract: This paper proposes a constant-loss (CL) wireless power transfer (WPT) system operating at 6.78 MHz for device-to-device(D2D) wireless charging applications, designed to maximize the available charging rate by fully utilizing the system’s physical thermal design. The system adopts a Series– Series (SS) compensation topology for its load-independent characteristics and a hybrid Class-ED power stage to achieve a high power rating with a low supply voltage. By monitoring both the input and output power and employing a closed-loop feedback control scheme, constant-loss charging can be maintained throughout the entire charging process. The proposed design is validated through simulation results of a wireless battery charger. The proposed CL charging scheme effectively exploits the allowable power dissipation, thereby approaching the theoretical maximum charging rate.

title: Thermal-Aware 3D-IC Floorplan Based On TSV-Coordination Simulated Annealing.
abstract: With the development of high-performance circuit systems, a surge in functional modules increases wirelength and chip temperature, degrading system performance. 3D integrated circuits (3D-IC) reduce overall area and total wirelength via vertical stacking and through-silicon vias (TSV), but their design suffers from more TSVs, longer wirelength and higher temperature due to heterogeneous integration. In this paper, we propose a three-stage optimization strategy based on simulated annealing (SA): layer assignment prioritizes minimizing cross-layer TSV number; intra-layer optimization sequentially optimizes module and TSV positions; thermal optimization introduces a 3D thermal clustering index to optimize overall system temperature. Experiments on the GSRC benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can significantly reduce the number of TSVs by 4%~33% and wirelength by 1%~12%, while achieving temperature performance comparable to advanced methods.

title: TLMALS: Tiny Language-Model Enhanced ALS via Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: Approximate computing is crucial for designing energy- and area-efficient hardware, yet existing methods often lack generality and global optimization capability. To overcome these limitations, we propose TLMALS-Tiny Language-Model Enhanced Approximate Logic Synthesis (ALS) via Reinforcement Learning. TLMALS represents circuits as textual sequences and employs a pretrained language model as the agent, transforming logic approximation into a language-understandable task and enabling semantic knowledge transfer from natural language to EDA. We design a bespoke tokenizer for circuit language and seamlessly embed the graph structure into the textual representation, breaking the long-standing barrier of fixed-node graphs that struggle with dynamic-node tasks. Reinforcement learning facilitates efficient exploration of approximation spaces beyond local optima. To address the weak interpretability issue of general approximate methods, a method-decoupled compensation mechanism adapts flexibly to error scenarios and restores accuracy. Experiments show that TLMALS reduces circuit area by 45.9% on average under 5% error rate.

title: A Challenge-Based-Learning System to Improve Education in Circuit and System Design.
abstract: In this paper, we present a challenge-based learning (CBL) system for education in circuit and system design. Within this system teachers implement circuit design challenges. Learners provide their own circuits as solutions. These solutions are automatically tested by the system using a test bench provided by the teacher. The test bench performs automatic measurements and derives scores based on test cases. We accumulate these scores e.g. in a figure of merit (FOM) and display them on a high score list to compare different learners’ solutions. In this way, we provide direct feedback, and engage and motivate learners in a competitive context. We implement the system using three main blocks: A Python application programming interface (API) to simulate the test benches using LTspice, a website as a user interface (UI) for teachers and learners and a database to store simulation files and data. We show, how to use the system on a circuit design example, and discuss various areas of application.
